items.description:
Validate a Python version specifier used in requirements files. Rules:
- It must start with one of the operators ==, >=, <=, >, <, != or ~=, with no spaces between the operator and the version.
- The version is one, two, or three dot-separated numeric components (each one or more digits, no leading zeros requirement).
- Optionally, a single pre-release suffix may follow: one of a, b, rc followed by digits, attached directly to the version with no separator.
- The string must contain nothing else.

In our JavaScript monorepo the package.json files declare dependency ranges that start with either a caret or a tilde, followed by a three-part version number made of digits separated by dots. There may be an optional pre-release tag at the end introduced by a hyphen, where the tag is dot-separated alphanumeric identifiers. We need to accept only those caret or tilde ranges, nothing else, so a build step can check that nobody used a bare version.

Our internal dependency scanner reads Python requirements files. Each line is a single requirement specifier and we must classify it before storing. Right now we only care about exact pins: the operator '===' followed immediately by a version that has at least one dot-separated numeric component, where each component is one or more digits. The version may end with an optional dot-separated pre-release or post-release marker made of letters and digits. The whole line must match; no trailing whitespace, comments, or extras.

We're writing a lint rule for package.json files in our monorepo. Any dependency range that uses a tilde must be flagged unless it is followed by a version with exactly three numeric parts and nothing else on the line. Versions with a leading zero in any part, prerelease tags, or build metadata are not allowed in this style, and neither are wildcards or x placeholders.

Accept a Python environment marker-style version comparison. The operator is one of the six comparison symbols, optionally preceded by whitespace. After the operator, optionally separated by whitespace, comes a version: either a major-only number, or a major and minor separated by a dot, or a full three-part dotted version. Each part is a non-negative integer with no leading zeros unless it is exactly zero. An optional pre-release of a, b, or rc followed by digits may be attached to the final numeric part without a separator. The string may end with trailing whitespace but nothing else.

The width must be between 640 and 7680 inclusive, and the height must be between 480 and 4320 inclusive. Exactly one 'x' (lowercase) separates the width and height. No spaces or other characters are allowed.

Validate a temperature string. It must start with a number (integer or decimal with up to two decimal places), followed by a space, then a unit: either '°C' for Celsius or '°F' for Fahrenheit. The unit is case-insensitive, but the degree symbol is optional? Actually, the degree symbol is required. We need to validate geographic coordinates entered by users for our mapping feature. The coordinate must be in degrees, minutes, and seconds format, with the hemisphere indicator (N/S/E/W) appended at the end. Degrees must be an integer from 0 to 180, minutes from 0 to 59, and seconds from 0 to 59. Each component must be two digits with leading zeros if necessary, separated by spaces. The hemisphere indicator is a single uppercase letter, but it must be consistent: for latitude, N or S; for longitude, E or W. items.description: A simplified five-field cron expression with fields for minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, separated by single spaces. Each field can contain digits, commas, hyphens, asterisks, and forward slashes, with no other characters.

Our commit messages must follow the Conventional Commits format: a type, an optional scope in parentheses, an optional exclamation mark for breaking changes, a colon and space, and a non-empty description. Types are feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, chore, ci, and build. The scope, if present, may contain any characters except parentheses and must not be empty. The description must not be empty.

Validate a five-field cron expression (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) separated by single spaces. Each field must be one of the following forms: a single number, a range (two numbers separated by a hyphen), a list of comma-separated numbers or ranges, or a step (a base number, range, or asterisk followed by a slash and a positive step number). Numbers must not have leading zeros unless the number is exactly 0. The minute field is 0–59, hour 0–23, day of month 1–31, month 1–12, day of week 0–6. Asterisk is allowed in any field, and in the day-of-week field 7 is also allowed (Sunday). No whitespace other than the single spaces separating fields.

Our pull request titles must start with a ticket key like ABC-123 followed by a colon and space, then a conventional commit type (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, test, or perf), an optional scope in parentheses, an optional exclamation mark, another colon and space, and a non-empty description. The whole title is case-sensitive.

Git branch names must use the format type/description. The type must be one of feature, bugfix, hotfix, release, or chore. The description must contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, and must not start or end with a hyphen. The whole branch name must not contain spaces.

Validate a standard Base64 encoded string as defined by RFC 4648 (not URL-safe).
- The string must be non-empty.
- It consists of ASCII letters, digits, '+', and '/'.
- Its length must be a multiple of 4.
- It may end with at most two '=' padding characters, and the total length must still be a multiple of 4.

Match a canonical Base64 string: every group of four characters is either four base64 alphabet characters, or three base64 alphabet characters followed by a single '=', or two base64 alphabet characters followed by '==', with no other padding and no characters after padding; the string must be non-empty.

A line of a CSV file containing exactly four fields separated by semicolons, where no field may itself contain a semicolon, a double quote, a carriage return, or a line feed, and empty fields are allowed except that the whole line must not be empty of fields.

Match a comma-separated list of one or more base-10 integers.
1. The list must be non-empty.
2. Items are separated by exactly one comma; no leading, trailing, or doubled commas.
3. Each integer may optionally be preceded by a single '+' or '-', must contain at least one digit, and must not have leading zeros unless it is exactly '0' (an optional sign is allowed before that zero).
4. No whitespace is permitted anywhere in the string.

Our API accepts image payloads as inline data URLs, and the image data portion is standard base64; the field must not be blank and must decode as valid base64 image bytes, so reject anything that is empty or not well-formed base64.

items.description: We ingest web server logs into our analytics pipeline and need to recognize the common combined log format lines coming from our Apache and nginx frontends. A valid line is an IP address (four dot-separated numbers from 0 to 255), followed by whitespace, a hyphen, whitespace, the remote user field which is either a hyphen or any run of non-whitespace characters, whitespace, a timestamp enclosed in square brackets, whitespace, then a quoted request line (which begins with an HTTP method, a space, a request target containing no spaces, a space, and an HTTP version like HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2), whitespace, a quoted status code of exactly three digits, whitespace, and a quoted response size which is either a hyphen or a run of digits. Everything else on the line is ignored.

Our error dashboard latches onto Java exception stack frames printed in application logs. Such a frame is a line that begins with optional leading whitespace, then the word 'at', then a single space, a fully qualified class or method name, a dot, the method name, an opening parenthesis, the source location (either a filename followed by a colon and a line number, or the word 'Unknown Source' or 'Native Method' without a line number), and a closing parenthesis. Anything after the closing parenthesis is ignored.

The status-page monitor reads the first line of each HTTP response. We only care about responses that indicate a problem on either the client or the server side, so we match a status line that starts at the beginning of the line with a three digit code whose first digit is 4 or 5, followed by a single space and a space-free reason phrase, and then the end of the line. The HTTP version that normally precedes the code does not matter to us, and any trailing text after the reason phrase means we should not flag the line.

Match a line that contains a stack trace frame of the form "at package.Class.method(File.java:123)", where the frame may have leading spaces and may appear anywhere in the line followed by arbitrary text.

We are building a log rotation size estimator for the CDN edge servers and need to identify each completed request record in the access log. A record is an IP address consisting of four dot-separated decimal numbers between 0 and 255, a single space, then a quoted request line made of an uppercase HTTP method, a space, a request target with no spaces or double quotes, a space, an HTTP version in the form HTTP/ followed by one digit, a dot, and one more digit, and a closing quote; then a single space, a three-digit status code, a single space, and the response time in milliseconds as one or more digits. The record ends immediately after the response time.

items.description:
US dollar amount format:
- Optional leading minus sign.
- Dollar sign followed by digits.
- Digits may include commas as thousands separators (groups of three).
- Optionally, a decimal point followed by exactly two digits (cents).
- No spaces allowed.
Examples: $1,234, $1,234.56, -$1,234.56.
If a comma is present, it must separate groups of exactly three digits.

Japanese yen amount:
- Digits only, no decimals.
- Must not start with a leading zero unless the amount is exactly zero.
- May include commas as thousands separators, which must appear in groups of three digits.
- Optionally prefixed by the yen sign ¥.
Examples: 1000, ¥1,000, 0, ¥0.

Accounting-style negative amount:
- The entire amount is enclosed in parentheses.
- Inside: optional currency symbol ($, €, or £), followed by digits.
- Digits may include commas as thousands separators (groups of three).
- Optionally, a decimal point and exactly two digits.
- No spaces are allowed.
Examples: ($1,234.56), (€500), (£1,000).

For our French e-commerce site, we need to accept prices in euros as commonly written in France: the amount uses a comma as the decimal separator and a space as the thousands separator (groups of three digits), the thousands separator is required for numbers with four or more digits, and the euro sign (€) is placed at the end after a space. The amount must have exactly two decimal places and no leading zeros unless the integer part is zero. Example: 1 234,56 €.

A currency amount consists of a three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in uppercase, followed by a space, then the numeric amount. The amount must have at least one digit before the decimal point and exactly two digits after the decimal point. The integer part may include commas as thousands separators, but only in groups of three digits, and must not have a leading zero unless it is zero. No spaces are allowed within the numeric part. Example: USD 1,234.56.

Match a Git branch name based on the conventional format: type/description. Type is one of feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, or chore. Description is lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, cannot start or end with a hyphen, and has no consecutive hyphens.

Tag: a colon followed by one or more word characters. Digest: an at sign followed by sha256: and exactly 64 hexadecimal digits. Tag and digest are mutually exclusive. The entire string must not exceed 255 characters.

A semantic pull request title must follow the format: type(scope): subject. Type is one of feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, or perf. Scope is optional, and if present must be enclosed in parentheses and contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters or hyphens. After the colon, a space, and then the subject must include a ticket key in the form of two or more uppercase letters, a hyphen, and one or more digits, followed by a colon and a space, and then one or more word characters (letters, digits, or underscores). items.description: A semantic PR title consists of a type, an optional scope in parentheses, a colon, a space, and a subject. - A single number within the field's valid range
- A comma-separated list of numbers within the range
- A range of two numbers within the range separated by a hyphen (start ≤ end)
- A step value: either * or a range followed by a slash and a positive integer (1–59)

items.description: A French postal code consists of exactly five digits. However, the first two digits correspond to the department number, which can be 01 to 95, or 2A or 2B for Corsica. Additionally, overseas departments and territories use three-digit department codes starting with 97 or 98, but for this validation we only consider metropolitan France and Corsica. So the postal code must start with either a two-digit number between 01 and 95, or the letters '2A' or '2B', followed by exactly three digits. No spaces or other characters are allowed.

A German IBAN (International Bank Account Number) has the following format: two uppercase letters 'DE' followed by two check digits (any two digits), then exactly 18 digits. The total length is 22 characters. No spaces or separators are allowed. Only the format is checked, not the validity of the check digits.

In our e-commerce checkout, we need to validate UK postcodes for shipping addresses. A UK postcode consists of two parts: the outward code and the inward code, separated by a space. The outward code can be 2 to 4 characters: it starts with one or two uppercase letters (the area), optionally followed by one or two digits (the district), and may optionally have a letter after the digits (the sector). The inward code is always three characters: one digit followed by two uppercase letters. The space between the outward and inward codes is mandatory. The entire postcode must be uppercase.

A credit card number must be exactly 16 digits. It may optionally be written in groups of four digits separated by a single space. The groups must be exactly four digits each, and there must be no leading or trailing spaces. So valid formats are either 16 consecutive digits, or four groups of four digits separated by single spaces.

We need to accept credit card numbers in our payment form. The numbers are 16 digits long, but customers often type them with spaces every four digits. We want to allow that, but only if the spaces are exactly every four digits and the total number of digits is still 16. No other separators (like dashes) are allowed, and there should be no extra spaces at the beginning or end.

items.description:
Validate an RFC 1123 hostname.
Rules:
1. The entire string must be 1 to 253 characters long.
2. It consists of one or more labels separated by dots.
3. Each label must be 1 to 63 characters long.
4. A label may contain letters (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and hyphens.

We need to validate MAC addresses entered in our device registration form. A valid MAC address consists of six pairs of hexadecimal digits. The pairs must be separated by a consistent delimiter: either a colon, a hyphen, or no delimiter at all. Mixed delimiters are not allowed. Case is not important.

Match a private IPv4 address. A private IPv4 address is a dotted-quad where each octet is a number from 0 to 255, and the address falls in one of these ranges: 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255, or 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255.

Our internal network scanner needs to record only private IPv4 addresses. A private IPv4 address is a standard dotted-decimal IPv4 address whose value falls within one of the private ranges: 10.0.0.0 through 10.255.255.255, 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255, or 192.168.0.0 through 192.168.255.255.

items.description: semantic pr title with a ticket key: starts with a conventional commit type (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, chore), followed by optional scope in parentheses (lowercase letters and hyphens), then a colon and space, then a ticket key in square brackets (uppercase letters, dash, digits), then a space, then a description starting with a lowercase letter and containing only letters, digits, spaces, and punctuation (no newline).

Docker image reference: the image name must consist of one or more lowercase alphanumeric segments separated by single dots, dashes, or underscores; an optional registry host (hostname with optional port) may precede the image name, separated by a slash; an optional tag may follow, separated by a colon, consisting of one or more word characters (letters, digits, underscore), dots, or dashes. No scheme, no spaces. The whole string must match.

A Kubernetes resource name must be a valid DNS subdomain: it consists of one or more lowercase alphanumeric labels separated by dots, where each label starts and ends with an alphanumeric character and may contain hyphens in between, and the total length is at most 253 characters. The name must not start or end with a hyphen or dot, and consecutive dots or hyphens are not allowed except as separators between labels? Actually hyphens are only inside labels, so consecutive hyphens are not allowed. The entire string must match this pattern.

conventional commits title: type(scope): subject where type is one of feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, chore, build, ci, or revert; scope is optional and if present is wrapped in parentheses and may contain letters, digits, and hyphens; immediately followed by a colon and a space; subject is any non-empty sequence of characters except line breaks.

A simplified five-field cron expression consists of five space-separated fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12), and day of week (0-6, where 0 is Sunday). Each field can be a single number, a range (two numbers separated by a hyphen), a comma-separated list of numbers or ranges, or an asterisk. Spaces separate fields. No step values or names. The whole string must match.

items.description: apache combined log line

Match a common log line (CLF) from Apache or nginx. It starts with the client IP address, followed by a space, the client identity (usually a hyphen), a space, the authenticated user (usually a hyphen), a space, then the date and time enclosed in square brackets. After another space comes the request line enclosed in double quotes, then a space, the HTTP status code (exactly three digits), a space, and the size of the response in bytes (digits or a hyphen).

A single line that looks like a Java stack trace frame: it starts with optional whitespace, then the word 'at', then whitespace, then a fully qualified method name (dot-separated identifiers), an opening parenthesis, followed by either 'Native Method', 'Unknown Source', a filename and line number, or just a filename, and finally a closing parenthesis.
error code ERR-123

The number can be an integer or a decimal, and must be larger than 1 (so 1.0, 1.00, etc., are not valid, but 1.1, 1.5, 2, 100 are). The duration can be embedded in any text.

items.description:
A line of a log is a stack-trace frame if and only if it satisfies all of these constraints:
1. The line may begin with optional whitespace.
2. It must then start with the word "at" followed by exactly one space.
3. After that come one or more package/class path segments separated by dots, where each segment is a non-empty sequence of word characters, then a dot, then the method name which is also a non-empty sequence of word characters. At least one dot is required in the qualified name.
4. Immediately after the method name there must be an opening parenthesis, then the source location, then a closing parenthesis at the end of the line. The source location is either the word "Native" and a following space and the word "Method", or a file name consisting of one or more word characters, a dot, and one or more word characters, followed by a colon and a line number of one or more digits.
5. Trailing whitespace is not allowed after the closing parenthesis.
Do not validate anything else about the frame.

We monitor API requests and want to automatically flag log lines that report a request that took longer than one second, so the reliability team can review them. A line qualifies when it contains a duration of the form "<number>ms" (one or more digits directly followed by the two letters ms, case-insensitive) whose numeric value is at least 1000, or "<number>s" (one or more digits, optionally a decimal part consisting of a dot and one or more digits, directly followed by the letter s, case-insensitive) whose numeric value is strictly greater than 1. A bare "1s" or "1.0s" does not qualify, but "1.5s", "2s" and "1000ms" do. The duration may appear anywhere in the line, and the surrounding text is unrestricted.
log line starting with WARN level, optional timestamp before it

Our analytics pipeline ingests web-server access logs from both Apache and nginx. We need a single check that decides whether a line is a valid access-log entry in the combined format: the client IP address, then an optional ident token (a dash when unknown), then an optional authenticated user token (also a dash when unknown), then a timestamp in square brackets, then the request line in double quotes, then the HTTP status code, then the response size in bytes, and finally an optional trailing quoted referrer and quoted user-agent. All tokens are separated by single spaces, and the line must contain nothing before the client IP or after the last allowed part. IP addresses may be IPv4 dotted quads (each octet 0-255) or IPv6 addresses in the usual colon-and-hex form. The request line is the method (uppercase letters), a space, the request target (any characters except double quotes and spaces), a space, and the protocol version of the form HTTP/x.y where x and y are digits. The timestamp has the form day/Mon/year:hour:minute:second followed by a space and a timezone offset such as +0200. The status code is three digits, and the size is either a dash or one or more digits. The referrer and user-agent, if present, are double-quoted and may not contain double quotes.

In our on-call dashboards we group log lines by severity, and the parser needs to recognize lines that begin with the error severity. A valid line starts with the literal word ERROR in uppercase, immediately followed by a colon and a single space, and then any non-empty message text that does not contain a newline. Nothing may precede the severity word.

items.description: We validate Docker image references in our deployment tool. The reference may optionally include a registry hostname (which can be localhost or a domain with dots and optional port) before the repository path. The repository name consists of lowercase alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, and hyphens, and may contain slashes for namespaces. An optional tag may follow a colon, consisting of one or more word characters (letters, digits, underscores) up to 128 characters. The tag is optional; if no tag is provided, it defaults to latest. The entire string must match this pattern.

We need to enforce a branch naming convention for our Git repositories. A valid branch name must start with a team identifier: either 'feature/', 'bugfix/', or 'hotfix/', followed by a short description. The short description must consist of one or more lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, and must not start or end with a hyphen, and must not contain two consecutive hyphens. The entire branch name must match this pattern.

We validate Kubernetes resource names for our internal deployment system. A valid name must be a lowercase DNS subdomain: it consists of one or more DNS labels separated by dots. Each label must start and end with an alphanumeric character (a-z or 0-9), and may contain hyphens in between. The total length must not exceed 253 characters. Additionally, the name must not start or end with a hyphen or dot, and must not contain two consecutive dots. The entire string must match this pattern.

We need to check npm package names in our dependency audit tool. A valid npm package name is either unscoped or scoped. An unscoped name is a string of one or more characters that are URL-safe: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, periods, or tildes. It must not start with a period or underscore. A scoped name starts with an '@' followed by a scope name (same URL-safe characters, but without periods? Actually scope names can include periods but must not start with a period or underscore), then a slash, then a package name (same rules as unscoped: URL-safe characters, not starting with period or underscore). The entire string must match this pattern.

We need to validate crontab expressions in our scheduler configuration. A valid expression consists of five fields separated by whitespace (spaces or tabs). Each field can be: a single number, a range (two numbers separated by a hyphen), a step (a range or asterisk followed by a slash and a number), or a comma-separated list of these. The allowed ranges for each field are: minute 0-59, hour 0-23, day of month 1-31, month 1-12, day of week 0-6. The entire string must match this pattern.

For our online community, we require a username that is at least 4 and at most 20 characters long. It should consist only of lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. This is to keep usernames simple and URL-friendly.
A valid username is between 5 and 15 characters long, may contain letters, numbers, dots, underscores, and hyphens, but it must not start or end with a dot, underscore, or hyphen.

Email address format (practical, not RFC-complete):
- One or more characters from [a-zA-Z0-9._%+-] before the @.
- Exactly one @ symbol.
- Domain part: one or more labels separated by dots; each label consists of one or more letters, digits, or hyphens, and must not start or end with a hyphen.

To keep it simple, we'll allow any sequence of allowed characters, including consecutive dots, but many practical ones do. However, the description says 'one or more characters from [a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]', so it allows consecutive dots. That's fine.)

- Allowed characters: uppercase letters (A-Z), lowercase letters (a-z), digits (0-9), and the special characters underscore (_), hyphen (-), and period (.).

- The username must not contain the sequence '123' anywhere.
Provide a regex that validates these rules for a single-line string.

items.description:
Validate a CSS class name that follows the BEM naming convention:
- The name consists of one or more blocks separated by double underscores (__) for elements and double hyphens (--) for modifiers.
- Each block, element, or modifier segment must be a non-empty string of lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, but must not start with a digit or a hyphen.
- The overall name must not end with a hyphen.
- Modifiers can be chained: block--modifier--submodifier is allowed.
- Elements and modifiers can be combined: block__element--modifier.
- Only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores (only as part of __ or --), and double underscores/double hyphens as separators are allowed. No uppercase letters, spaces, or other punctuation.
- The entire string must match exactly (no leading/trailing whitespace).

Match a JavaScript import statement that imports the default export from a module whose name is exactly 'my-module'. The statement must start with the keyword 'import', followed by whitespace, then the identifier 'my-module' (as a string literal in single or double quotes), and end with a semicolon. The module name must be exactly 'my-module', no extra characters or paths. The import statement must be on a single line.

Validate a variable name that is either snake_case (all lowercase words separated by single underscores) or SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (all uppercase words separated by single underscores). Additional rules:
- The name must start and end with a letter (a-z or A-Z).
- Words may contain digits, but a word cannot start with a digit.
- Consecutive underscores are not allowed.
- No leading or trailing underscores.
- The entire string must match, no whitespace or other characters.

We need to enforce that all JavaScript variable names in our codebase follow camelCase. A valid camelCase name starts with a lowercase letter (a-z), followed by any number of letters (a-z, A-Z) and digits (0-9), and does not contain underscores, hyphens, or other special characters. It must not start with a digit or uppercase letter. The entire string must be a single word with no spaces.

Validate an environment variable name. Rules:
- The name must consist only of uppercase letters (A-Z), digits (0-9), and underscores (_).
- It must not start with a digit.
- It must not contain lowercase letters, spaces, or any other special characters.
- The entire string must match exactly, with no leading or trailing whitespace.

The timestamp must have the date (four-digit year, two-digit month, two-digit day) and time (two-digit hour, minute, second) separated by a 'T', followed immediately by a 'Z' to indicate UTC. We need to validate that each line in our web server access log follows the standard Common Log Format. The line must start with the client's IP address, which can be either IPv4 (four numbers separated by dots) or IPv6 (groups of hexadecimal digits separated by colons). After the IP, there should be a space, then the remote logname (a hyphen if unknown, or a word), another space, the authenticated username (a hyphen if unknown, or a word), another space, followed by the date and time in square brackets, and then a quoted request line. The request line must be in the format: HTTP method (letters), space, request URI (any characters except space), space, HTTP version (like HTTP/1.1). After the quoted request, there should be a space, a three-digit HTTP status code, a space, and the response size in bytes (a number or a hyphen). The line should end there, though extra fields may follow in some logs; we only care about the standard fields.

items.description: Our desktop app needs to accept a Windows file path from the user. A valid path starts with a drive letter (a single letter, uppercase or lowercase) followed by a colon and a backslash. After that it may contain zero or more path segments separated by backslashes; each segment must be one or more characters that are not a backslash or any of the following: < > : " | ? * (control characters are also not allowed). The path must not end with a backslash unless it is just the drive root, i.e., the drive letter, colon, and trailing backslash with nothing after it.

In our file-upload UI, we treat any file whose name begins with a dot as a hidden file. The user enters just the file name (no directories). A hidden dotfile name must start with a dot, followed by one or more characters that are not a slash, backslash, or a NUL character. The name must not be just a dot or two dots.

Validate a file name (not a full path) that may contain letters, digits, spaces, dots, hyphens, underscores, and parentheses, but must not contain any of the characters: / \ : * ? " < > |. It must have at least one character, cannot start or end with a space, and cannot be exactly '.' or '..'.

When users name a configuration file, we require it to be a hidden file: its name must begin with a dot and then contain only lowercase letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens. The dot is mandatory and must be followed by at least one of those characters.

We need to match test file names used by our test runner. A valid test file name must end with either '.spec' or '.test' followed by a JavaScript or TypeScript extension: '.js', '.ts', '.jsx', or '.tsx'. The base name (everything before the final suffix) must be one or more characters that are not slashes, backslashes, or a NUL character. The match is case-sensitive. For example, 'foo.spec.ts' and 'bar.test.jsx' are valid, but 'foo.spec' (no extension), 'foo.test.js.map', and 'foo.spec.tsx.bak' are not.

items.description:
Validate an npm package name. Rules:
- The name is either unscoped or scoped.
- An unscoped name starts with a lowercase letter, then may contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, or dots. It cannot end with a dot.
- A scoped name starts with '@', followed by a scope segment, then '/', then a package segment.
- The scope segment and package segment each start with a lowercase letter, may contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, or dots, and cannot end with a dot.
- The overall name length is 1 to 214 characters for unscoped, or 1 to 214 characters for the part after '@' for scoped.
- URL-unsafe characters are not allowed.
- Only the format is checked; the name is not checked against the npm registry.

Match a Docker image reference with an optional tag. The reference consists of a repository name, optionally followed by a colon and a tag. The repository name is a sequence of path components separated by slashes; each component contains lowercase letters, digits, periods, underscores, or hyphens, and must not start or end with a period or hyphen. The tag, if present, is a string of letters, digits, underscores, periods, or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, with length 1 to 128 characters.

We enforce Conventional Commits for all commit titles. A valid title starts with a type (one of: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert), optionally followed by a scope in parentheses containing one or more lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens. Then a colon and a space, followed by a description that is at least one character and does not start with a space. The description may contain any characters except line breaks. No breaking-change indicator is required.

Our team uses Conventional Commits, and we need a stricter check for a title on a single line. The type must be one of: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. An optional scope in parentheses may contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, and slashes, but must not start or end with a hyphen or slash. After the optional scope, there must be either a colon and a space followed by a description that does not start with a space, or an exclamation mark before the colon to indicate a breaking change, also followed by a colon, a space, and a description that does not start with a space. The description may contain any characters except line breaks. The entire title must not contain line breaks.

Our pull request titles must follow semantic conventions and include a ticket key. A valid title starts with a type (one of: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert), optionally followed by a scope in parentheses containing one or more lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens. Then a colon, a space, and a description. The description must begin with a ticket key: an uppercase project prefix (2 to 10 uppercase letters), a hyphen, and a number (1 to 6 digits), followed by a space and at least one non-space character. The ticket key may be at the very start of the description or immediately after the colon-space; no other position is allowed.

items.description:
Validate an ISO 8601 timestamp. Rules:
- Date part: exactly four digits for the year, a hyphen, exactly two digits for the month, a hyphen, exactly two digits for the day.
- A literal uppercase 'T' separates date and time.
- Time part: exactly two digits for the hour, a colon, exactly two digits for the minute, a colon, exactly two digits for the second.
- Timezone part: either a literal 'Z' (UTC), or a sign ('+' or '-') followed by exactly two digits for the offset hour, a colon, and exactly two digits for the offset minute.
No validation of calendar correctness (e.g. month ranges) is required.

Our audit log ingestion pipeline expects every event timestamp to be written in the standard international format used by our APIs: a full calendar date (four-digit year, two-digit month, two-digit day), followed by the letter T, then the wall-clock time as two-digit hour, minute and second separated by colons, and finally a timezone designator which is either the letter Z or a signed hour:minute offset. Only the shape of the string matters; we do not check that the date actually exists on the calendar.

Accept a 24-hour clock time. The hour is two digits from 00 to 23, the minute is two digits from 00 to 59, and the seconds are optional: when present they are introduced by a colon and are two digits from 00 to 59. No other characters are allowed.
iso 8601 utc-ish timestamp: yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss then either Z or +hh:mm or -hh:mm, nothing else

The compliance team exports records to partners, and the partner system rejects the whole file unless each record's creation time is in the agreed interchange format: a date with four-digit year, two-digit month and two-digit day, a capital T, then hour, minute and second each as two digits separated by colons, and a timezone indicator that is either Z or a plus-or-minus offset written as two-digit hours, a colon and two-digit minutes. Only the format is checked, not whether the date or time values are real.

A valid string is a standard Base64 encoding:
- It consists only of the characters A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '+', and '/'.
- Its length is a multiple of 4.
- It may end with one or two padding '=' characters to make the length a multiple of 4; padding only appears at the end and only if the encoded data length would otherwise not be a multiple of 4.

Our internal system uses calendar-based versioning for monthly releases. A version string must be in the format YYYY.MM where YYYY is a four-digit year (no leading zeros) and MM is a two-digit month from 01 to 12. There should be exactly one dot between the year and month. Only digits are allowed. For example, 2024.06 is valid, but 24.6 and 2024.13 are not.

items.description: Our signup flow accepts only company web addresses under the .io top-level domain. A valid value consists of one or more labels separated by dots, ending with the io TLD: each label must start and end with an alphanumeric character, may contain alphanumeric characters and hyphens in between, and the .io suffix is mandatory. Domain labels are case-insensitive and each label must be between 1 and 63 characters long. Do not allow any other top-level domain.

A URL path with no query string and no fragment. Constraints:
1. The path starts with a forward slash.
2. It contains one or more path segments separated by single forward slashes; segments may be empty, so a trailing slash is permitted.
3. Only these characters are allowed anywhere in the path: letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, dot, tilde, percent sign, plus and forward slash.
4. The path must not contain a question mark or hash.
5. The path may not be longer than 2000 characters.

The analytics dashboard lets users paste the path portion of a URL into a filter box, and we want to reject anything that isn't a clean path. The value must begin with a slash, each segment is separated by a single slash, and no segment may be empty except that the whole path may optionally end with one trailing slash. Segments can use letters (any case), digits, hyphens, underscores, periods, tildes or percent signs, plus and equals signs are not allowed. Query strings and fragments are not accepted, so a question mark or a hash anywhere makes the value invalid.

In the sitemap builder, we need to validate the path component of URLs, such as category or article paths. A path must start with a slash, may consist of one or more segments separated by slashes, and must not be empty overall. Each segment is made of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores and dots. The only exception is that a segment may contain an at-sign as long as it is not the first character of that segment. A trailing slash is not allowed, and neither query strings nor fragments may be present.

Our link checker needs to accept web addresses that begin with either the http or https scheme, followed by a host, an optional port, and an optional path. The scheme must be followed by ://; the host must be composed of dot-separated labels of alphanumeric characters and hyphens, with the last label at least two characters long, and it may not start with a hyphen. A port, if present, is written as a colon followed by one to five digits. The path, if present, starts with a slash and then contains any non-space characters. Whitespace is not allowed anywhere in the address.

items.description:
A camelCase identifier as used for variable and function names.

Rules:
1. Starts with a lowercase ASCII letter a-z.
2. The remaining characters are ASCII letters a-z or A-Z, or digits 0-9.
3. No underscores, no dashes, no leading or trailing digits, and digits may not be adjacent to a digit... in fact, digits may appear anywhere after the first character, but every uppercase letter must be immediately followed by at least one lowercase letter (no two uppercase letters in a row).
4. The entire string must match; no whitespace allowed.
5. Length is 1 to 40 characters.

Our code review bot scans source files for leftover work notes and flags them in the pull request. We only care about lines that are entirely a work note: an optional indentation of spaces or tabs, then comment markers, a task keyword, and the note text. The keyword must be one of TODO, FIXME, or XXX in capitals, followed by a colon or a space (the colon or space is required). After that separator there must be at least one non-whitespace character of note text, and the note text runs to the end of the line. The comment markers may be either two slashes, a hash, or two dashes, followed by optional spaces. Lines with trailing whitespace after the note text are valid. No other content is allowed on the line.

Validate a JavaScript identifier, restricted to the ASCII subset.

- First character: letter, underscore, or dollar sign.
- Subsequent characters: letter, digit, underscore, or dollar sign.
- Empty strings are not allowed.

We generate CSS class names from page section titles, and designers want them all in the lowercase-with-dashes style. A generated name is accepted only if it is all lowercase letters and digits, separated into one or more words by single dashes, with no dash at the start or end and no two dashes in a row. Each word must start with a letter, so the name cannot start with a digit or dash. Hit names longer than sixty characters are rejected by the build step.

We let plugin authors choose the name of the JavaScript function they expose. Before registering it we must reject names that could break the runtime, so a name is only accepted if it is a valid JavaScript identifier in the ASCII sense but is not one of the reserved words that would be a syntax error when used as a variable name: break, case, catch, class, const, continue, debugger, default, delete, do, else, enum, export, extends, false, finally, for, function, if, import, in, instanceof, new, null, return, super, switch, this, throw, true, try, typeof, var, void, while, with, yield. Identifiers may start with a letter, underscore, or dollar sign and then contain those plus digits. Matching is case-sensitive, so a capitalized version such as If is fine. Reject the empty string as well.

items.description: A valid branch name must follow these rules: it must start with an optional type prefix (one of feat, fix, hotfix, release, chore, docs, refactor, test, ci, build, perf, style, or revert) followed by a forward slash, but the prefix and slash are optional; after the optional prefix, the name must start with a ticket key consisting of one or more uppercase letters, a hyphen, and one or more digits (e.g., ABC-123), followed by a hyphen; then a description part that consists of one or more segments separated by hyphens, where each segment contains only lowercase letters, digits, or dots, must start and end with a lowercase letter or digit, and must not contain two consecutive dots; the entire branch name must not contain spaces, uppercase letters (except in the ticket key), or any characters other than those specified; additionally, the branch name must not start or end with a hyphen or contain two consecutive hyphens.

We need to validate Docker image references in our deployment configuration. The image reference should consist of a repository path followed by an optional tag. The repository path may contain lowercase letters, digits, and separators such as periods, underscores, and hyphens (but must not start or end with a separator, and separators cannot be consecutive). Optionally, a registry hostname may be specified before the repository path, separated by a slash; the registry hostname may contain lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and optional port number after a colon. The tag, if present, must be preceded by a colon and consist of word characters, dots, or hyphens. The total length must not exceed 255 characters.

A semantic pull request title must begin with one of the following types followed by a colon and a space: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. After the colon and space, there must be a ticket key in the format of two to four uppercase letters, a hyphen, and one to five digits. The ticket key must be followed by another colon and space, and then a non-empty description that contains at least one character. The description may include any characters except line breaks. The entire title must not exceed 72 characters.
semantic pr title with ticket key, e.g. feat: ABC-123: add new feature

Our Kubernetes resource names must be valid according to the platform's naming rules. They must be 63 characters or fewer, consist only of lowercase alphanumeric characters or '-', start and end with an alphanumeric character, and must not contain two consecutive hyphens. Names must be unique within a namespace, but we only need to check the format.

items.description: We need a validation for the weight field in our shipping system. Customers can enter the weight in kilograms or grams. The value must be a number (integer or decimal) followed by either 'kg' or 'g', case-insensitive. No spaces are allowed between the number and the unit. The number part can optionally have a decimal part with a dot. Examples of valid entries: '5kg', '3.5kg', '500g', '0.75g'. Invalid: '5 kg', '3.5', 'kg5', '5KG '.
latitude between -90 and 90, optional decimal up to any digits

The string must represent image dimensions in the format WIDTHxHEIGHT, where WIDTH and HEIGHT are positive integers (no leading zeros, except the number 0 itself is not allowed). There must be exactly one lowercase 'x' between them. No other characters are allowed. Examples: '1920x1080', '640x480', '1x1'. Invalid: '1920X1080', '1920 x 1080', '01920x1080', '1920x', 'x1080'.

In our file upload interface, users must specify the maximum file size. The value should be a positive integer (no decimals) followed by a unit: KB, MB, or GB, case-insensitive. No spaces between number and unit. Examples: '100KB', '2MB', '1GB'. Invalid: '100 KB', '2.5MB', '0KB', 'KB'.

A longitude in decimal degrees. Must be a number between -180 and 180 inclusive. The number may have an optional sign ('+' or '-'), no sign means positive. The integer part can be 1 to 3 digits; if it is 180, the decimal part must be all zeros (or absent). The decimal part is optional and if present must be a dot followed by one or more digits. Examples: '0', '-180', '+180.0', '45.123', '-179.9999'. Invalid: '180.1', '-180.0001', '181', '45.'.

slots.intent: line mentioning a duration above one second
log line starting with a given level
log line with an ISO timestamp prefix

Apache or nginx access log line

items.description: A log line is valid if it contains a duration value that is strictly greater than one second. The duration is written as a time quantity with a numeric part and a unit. The numeric part is one or more digits, optionally followed by a decimal part: a dot and one or more digits. The unit is either 'ms' for milliseconds, 's' for seconds, 'm' for minutes, or 'h' for hours. The numeric part may be preceded by one or more whitespace characters, but a duration that is exactly one second (e.g., '1s' or '1.00s') or less must not be considered valid. The duration can appear anywhere in the line; the line may contain other text before or after.
log line starting with a given level (ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG) followed by a space

We need to identify log entries that begin with a timestamp in the ISO 8601 format. The timestamp must be at the very start of the line and consist of a four-digit year, a hyphen, a two-digit month, a hyphen, a two-digit day, the letter 'T', a two-digit hour, a colon, a two-digit minute, a colon, a two-digit second, and a timezone designator. The timezone designator is either 'Z' or a plus or minus sign followed by a two-digit hour, a colon, and a two-digit minute. The timestamp may be optionally followed by a space, but that space is not required.
line containing a stack trace frame

We need to parse standard access log entries from our web servers, which may be Apache or nginx. Each entry is a single line that starts with the client's IP address, followed by a space, then the remote logname (a hyphen if not available), a space, and then the authenticated user (a hyphen if not available). After another space, the timestamp appears enclosed in square brackets. The timestamp format is day/month/year:hour:minute:second timezone, where day is two digits, month is three letters, year is four digits, and timezone is a plus or minus sign followed by four digits. This is followed by a space and then the request line in double quotes. The request line consists of an HTTP method (one or more uppercase letters), a space, the request target (one or more characters that are not spaces or double quotes), a space, and the HTTP version (the string 'HTTP/' followed by one or more digits, a dot, and one or more digits), all inside the double quotes. French SIRET or SIREN number in the format used for official identification:

- SIRET: exactly 14 digits (which is the SIREN plus a 5-digit NIC).
The digits may optionally be separated by single spaces in groups of 3, e.g., '123 456 789' for SIREN or '123 456 789 00012' for SIRET? Actually the specification says: the digits can be grouped by spaces in blocks of 3, except the last block which may have 3 or 5 digits? No, that's not standard. Let's re-read: The format is: 9 or 14 digits, optionally with spaces every 3 digits from the right? That would be unusual. Typically SIRET is written as 3-3-3-5 with spaces. But to keep it consistent, we'll define: the number is a sequence of 9 or 14 digits, and it may contain spaces. If spaces are present, they must separate groups of exactly 3 digits, except that the final group may have 3 or 5 digits? Actually, if we have 9 digits, it can be '123 456 789' (3 groups of 3). If we have 14 digits, it could be '123 456 789 00012' (groups: 3,3,3,5) or '123 456 789 012 345'? No, 14 digits with groups of 3 would be 3+3+3+3+2, not standard. The official SIRET is often written with spaces after every 3 digits from the left, resulting in groups of 3,3,3,3,2 for 14 digits, but that's not common. Actually, the official format for SIRET is 14 digits, often written as SIREN (9 digits) followed by NIC (5 digits), with spaces: '123 456 789 00012'. That's 3-3-3-5. So we'll allow that.

We need to specify: The input is either:
- 9 digits (optionally with spaces: groups of 3 digits separated by single spaces, exactly 3 groups).
- 14 digits, optionally with spaces: either groups of 3,3,3,5 (i.e., three groups of 3 digits, then a group of 5 digits) separated by single spaces, or no spaces at all? Actually, if spaces are present, they must follow the grouping pattern: for 9 digits: XXX XXX XXX; for 14 digits: XXX XXX XXX XXXXX.

So the regex should accept:
- 9 digits: ^\d{9}$ or ^\d{3} \d{3} \d{3}$
- 14 digits: ^\d{14}$ or ^\d{3} \d{3} \d{3} \d{5}$

But the description says 'The digits may optionally be separated by single spaces in groups of 3, except that for SIRET the last group has 5 digits.' That matches our pattern.

Let's formalize:

A SIREN is exactly 9 digits, optionally written as three groups of 3 digits separated by single spaces.
A SIRET is exactly 14 digits, optionally written as three groups of 3 digits followed by a group of 5 digits, all separated by single spaces.

So the regex: /^(?:\d{9}|\d{3} \d{3} \d{3}|\d{14}|\d{3} \d{3} \d{3} \d{5})$/

For internal network configuration, we only accept private IPv4 addresses. items.description: Our dependency checker needs to accept semantic version range strings that specify a caret or tilde range. The string must start with either a caret or a tilde, followed immediately by a semantic version in the form major.minor.patch. Major, minor, and patch must each be a number with no leading zeros unless the number is exactly zero. No other characters or spaces are allowed.

The release pipeline requires that every version string stored in the build metadata be a valid semantic version. A valid version has three numeric components separated by dots: major, minor, and patch. Each component must be a non-negative integer without leading zeros (except the single digit zero). No prerelease, build metadata, or additional characters are permitted.

Match a Python version specifier that starts with a comparison operator (==, !=, <=, >=, <, or >) followed by a version number consisting of one to three dot-separated numeric parts (major, minor, patch). Each numeric part must be a non-negative integer without leading zeros unless it is exactly zero. The specifier may optionally end with a pre-release segment: a hyphen followed by one of the identifiers a, b, or rc (optionally with a dot) and a numeric serial without leading zeros unless it is zero.

Our deployment system needs to recognize version tags for releases. The tags follow the pattern v followed by one to three dot-separated numeric parts (major, minor, patch), where each part is a non-negative integer without leading zeros unless it is zero. The tag can optionally end with -beta followed by a dot and a numeric build number without leading zeros unless it is zero. No other suffixes or characters are allowed.

The package manager must validate Python version specifiers that use the compatible-release operator ~=. The specifier starts with ~= followed by a version with at least two numeric parts (major.minor) and an optional third part (patch), separated by dots. Each numeric part must be a non-negative integer without leading zeros unless it is exactly zero. The version may optionally end with a pre-release segment: a hyphen followed by one of a, b, or rc (optionally followed by a dot) and a numeric serial without leading zeros unless it is zero. The string must contain no other characters or whitespace.

items.description: Our support dashboard groups incoming events by severity. An accepted event line must begin with a severity label in capitals: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR or FATAL. The label is immediately followed by a single colon and a space, and after that any content may appear, including nothing at all. The whole line must be checked; leading spaces or tabs before the label make a line invalid.

A log line counts as containing an error code when a bracketed code made of exactly three uppercase letters followed by a hyphen and four digits appears anywhere in the line. The surrounding text must not contain a letter or digit immediately before the opening bracket or immediately after the closing bracket, so that longer codes and partial matches are ignored.

We ingest web server logs from both our Apache and nginx hosts into the analytics pipeline. Each accepted line is a plain HTTP request record in the common log style: a client address, a space, a hyphen, a space, a username token, a space, then a timestamp in square brackets, a space, and the quoted request line. We only need the shape of the line, not the individual field contents.

The performance team wants to flag slow requests in our logs. A line is relevant when it mentions a duration of one second or longer. Durations are written as a whole number of seconds using the unit suffix s, or as a whole number of milliseconds using the suffix ms, optionally separated from the number by a single space. A bare number without a unit is never a duration. The number and its unit may appear anywhere in the line.

Log line validation, level-prefixed form. Constraints:
1. The line must start with one of the levels DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, FATAL, written in uppercase, at the very beginning of the string.
2. The level is followed by optional spaces and an optional tab-indented prefix.
3. After the level the line may be empty.
4. If not empty, the remainder may be any characters, and may itself end with a colon-separated detail. Trailing spaces are permitted.

items.description: Our scheduler accepts five-field cron expressions where each field is a comma-separated list of items. An item is either a single number within the field's allowed range or a wildcard. Minutes and hours are zero-padded to two digits, day-of-month and month are zero-padded to two digits, and day-of-week is a single digit from zero to six or a three-letter day abbreviation. No other special characters or step/range syntax is supported.

Validate a Conventional Commits 1.0.0 commit title (the subject line). The title must contain a type, an optional scope, an optional breaking-change indicator, a colon and a space, and a non-empty description. The type must be one of: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. The scope, if present, is a non-empty sequence of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores, enclosed in parentheses. The breaking-change indicator is an exclamation mark immediately after the type or scope and before the colon. The description must not be empty and must not consist solely of whitespace. Only the first line of the commit message is considered; the description therefore must not contain line breaks.

A Kubernetes resource name must be a valid DNS label: it must consist only of lowercase alphanumeric characters or hyphens, must start and end with an alphanumeric character, and must be at most 63 characters long.

We enforce a PR title convention for our GitHub repos. Every pull request title must start with a ticket key from our Jira. A ticket key is an uppercase project code (two to ten letters), followed by a hyphen, followed by one to six digits. After the ticket key, there must be a colon and a space, followed by a short description of at least one non-space character. The description part must not contain a colon, because that would be confused with the separator.

Our registry accepts npm package names that are either unscoped or scoped. An unscoped name is a non-empty sequence of characters that must not start with a dot or underscore and must not contain uppercase letters. A scoped name starts with an @, followed by a non-empty scope name that also must not start with a dot or underscore and must not contain uppercase letters, then a slash, then a non-empty package name with the same character restrictions. Names must not contain spaces and must not exceed 214 characters.

Validate a Windows absolute path. Rules:
1. The string starts with a drive letter, which must be a single uppercase or lowercase letter A–Z, followed by a colon.
2. After the colon there is a backslash.
3. Then one or more path segments separated by single backslashes. Each segment consists of one or more characters that are not a backslash, a forward slash, a colon, an asterisk, a question mark, a double quote, a less-than sign, a greater-than sign, a pipe, or a control character.

Our desktop client logs which file a user opened, and a field in the telemetry event has to hold the Windows absolute path to that file. Only paths that start with a drive letter (a colon then a backslash after it) and that are complete — no trailing backslash after the last file name — count as valid; a path name part may not contain the usual forbidden Windows characters, which are the backslash itself, forward slash, colon, asterisk, question mark, double quote, angle brackets, pipe, or any control character.

Marketing drops daily report files into a folder and the uploader has to accept only the ones named with the reporting date up front. The date is written as four digits for the year, a hyphen, two digits for the month and two digits for the day, immediately followed by an underscore and then a file name made of letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, ending in a .csv extension. The extension should be accepted in upper or lower case, and the whole name must match exactly — no extra text before the date or after the extension.

Each invoice scan is stored under a file name that begins with the date the document was received in year-month-day form using four digits for the year, a dash, two digits for the month, and a dash followed by two digits for the day, and that date must be followed directly by an underscore and then the customer's account reference, which is a non-empty run of lowercase letters and digits. After the reference the name ends either with a single dot and a lowercase extension of two to four letters, or with a version suffix made of a dash followed by one or more digits, then a dot, then that same two-to-four-letter lowercase extension. Nothing else may appear before the date or after the extension, and a name that only looks like a date but has the wrong number of digits must be rejected.

The pre-release part starts with a hyphen and consists of dot-separated identifiers that are either numeric or alphanumeric (may include hyphens and dots). The string starts with P, and if there are time components (hours, minutes, or seconds), a T must separate the date part from the time part. Each component is an integer (no leading plus or minus, no decimal point) followed by its designator: Y, M, D, H, M, or S. The M for months and the M for minutes are distinguished by their position relative to T. For example, P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S is valid, but P1Y2M3D4H is not because it lacks the T before the time part.

The appointment booking form needs to validate the time entered by users in a 12-hour format with AM/PM. The AM/PM indicator can be in uppercase or lowercase, but must be consistent (either both uppercase or both lowercase). Leading zeros are allowed for the hour, but not required. For example, '9:30 AM' and '12:00 pm' are valid, but '0:30 AM' and '13:00 PM' are not.

Accept a time in 24-hour format. The format is HH:MM or HH:MM:SS. HH is two digits from 00 to 23. MM is two digits from 00 to 59. SS, if present, is two digits from 00 to 59. The colon separators are required. Leading zeros are mandatory for all components. No other characters are allowed.

The date part consists of years (Y), months (M), and days (D) in that order; each component is an integer (no sign, no decimal) followed by its designator. The time part is introduced by 'T' and consists of hours (H), minutes (M), and seconds (S) in that order; each component is an integer. At least one component (date or time) must be present. Each component may appear at most once. The 'T' is required if and only if there is at least one time component. No other characters are allowed. For example, 'P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S' is valid, 'P1Y2M3D' is valid, 'PT4H' is valid, but 'P' alone is invalid, and 'P1Y2M3D4H' is invalid because it lacks 'T' before the time part.

items.description:
Validate a standard Base64 encoding of a non-empty byte sequence, as produced by btoa/atob conventions. Rules:
1. The string consists only of A–Z, a–z, 0–9, '+', and '/'.
2. The length is a multiple of 4.
3. Content is split into 4-character groups; padding '=' appears only at the very end, either once or twice.
4. If there is a single '=' at the end, the preceding character must encode exactly 2 bits that are zero: the second-to-last character must be one of A, E, I, M, Q, U, Y, c, g, k, o, s, w, 0, 4, 8 (its low 4 bits are zero... precisely, its value mod 16 must be 0).
5. If there are two '=' at the end, the character before them must encode exactly 4 bits that are zero: it must be one of A, Q, g, w.
6. No padding is allowed if the encoded data length is already a multiple of 3 bytes (i.e., padding only when needed), and an unpadded remainder of 1 character is invalid.
Only the encoding format is checked, not any decoded payload semantics.

items.description: Our monitoring tool scans application log lines for slow requests. A line qualifies if it contains a duration value greater than one second. Durations are expressed as a number with exactly three decimal places followed by 'ms', e.g., milliseconds. The number can be an integer part with any number of digits (at least one) and must be strictly greater than 1000. The duration appears anywhere in the line; the line may contain other text before and after it. For example, 'Request took 1234.567ms' should match, but 'Request took 1000.000ms' should not.

Validate that a log line is a well-formed Apache or nginx combined access log entry. The line must follow the Combined Log Format: the client IP address, followed by a space, a hyphen, a space, the remote user (a hyphen if not authenticated), a space, then the timestamp in square brackets. The timestamp must be in the format day/month/year:hour:minute:second timezone, where day is two digits, month is a three-letter English abbreviation (case-sensitive, first letter uppercase, rest lowercase), year is four digits, hour is two digits (00-23), minute is two digits (00-59), second is two digits (00-59), and timezone is a plus or minus sign followed by four digits. After the timestamp and a space, the request line appears in double quotes: the HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, or PATCH), a space, the request URI (any characters except double quote), a space, and the HTTP version (HTTP/1.0, HTTP/1.1, or HTTP/2). Then a space, the status code (three digits), a space, and the response size (either a hyphen or one or more digits). Then a space, the referrer in double quotes (any characters except double quote, or a hyphen), a space, and the user agent in double quotes (any characters except double quote, or a hyphen). The entire line must match exactly; no extra characters before or after.

The system must recognize log lines that start with a severity level. A valid line begins with one of the exact strings 'INFO:', 'WARN:', or 'ERROR:' (case-sensitive, followed by a colon) at the very beginning of the line. After the colon, there must be at least one whitespace character, and then any non-empty message. The rest of the line can contain any characters. Only lines that strictly follow this pattern should be considered valid.

Identify log lines that report an operation taking more than one second. The line must contain a duration expressed in milliseconds with exactly three decimal places, followed by the unit 'ms' (case-insensitive). The number part must have at least one digit before the decimal point and exactly three digits after. The duration must be strictly greater than 1000.000 milliseconds. The duration can appear anywhere in the line. For example, a line with '1500.000ms' should match, but '1000.000ms' should not. The rest of the line is unrestricted.

Validate that a log line begins with a log level indicator. The line must start with one of the following level tags, exactly as written, case-sensitive: 'DEBUG', 'INFO', 'WARNING', 'ERROR', or 'CRITICAL'. Each tag must be followed by a space, then a colon, then a space, and then at least one non-whitespace character (the log message). After that, the line may contain any additional characters. The entire line must match this pattern from start to end; no leading whitespace is allowed.

We need to validate that the input matches this format: it starts with P, followed by optional number of years (Y), months (M), days (D), and then optionally T followed by hours (H), minutes (M), and seconds (S). Users can use either slashes or dashes as separators, but they must be consistent throughout the date (i.e., all slashes or all dashes). items.description: Validate a hostname according to RFC 1123. The hostname must be 1 to 253 characters total. It consists of one or more labels separated by dots. Each label must be 1 to 63 characters, start and end with a letter or digit, and may contain letters, digits, and hyphens in between. The entire hostname must not start or end with a dot, and there must not be two consecutive dots. No trailing dot is allowed. Only ASCII letters (case-insensitive), digits, hyphens, and dots are permitted.

Validate an IPv4 address. It consists of four decimal numbers separated by dots. Each number must be an integer between 0 and 255, inclusive. Leading zeros are not allowed unless the number is exactly '0'.

We need to validate the CIDR notation field for network configuration. It should be an IPv4 address followed by a slash and a subnet mask length between 0 and 32. The IPv4 address must be four decimal numbers separated by dots, each between 0 and 255, with no leading zeros unless the number is 0. The prefix length must be an integer from 0 to 32 with no leading zeros unless it is 0.

In our log analysis tool, we need to extract and validate IPv4 addresses that appear anywhere as a substring. An IPv4 address is four decimal numbers separated by dots, each between 0 and 255. Leading zeros are not allowed unless the number is exactly 0. The address must not be part of a larger string of digits or dots; that is, it must not be preceded or followed by a digit or a dot. However, it can be surrounded by other characters like spaces, letters, or punctuation.

Validate a private IPv4 address. The allowed ranges are:
- 10.0.0.0 to 10.255.255.255
- 172.16.0.0 to 172.31.255.255
- 192.168.0.0 to 192.168.255.255
Each octet must be a decimal number between 0 and 255. Leading zeros are not allowed unless the number is exactly 0. The four octets are separated by dots. No other ranges are permitted.

A Windows path with a drive letter must satisfy all of the following:

items.description: Match a single line of a Java-style stack trace frame. Valid lines must satisfy all of the following: (1) the line starts with optional leading whitespace followed by the text "at "; (2) after that comes a fully qualified method reference consisting of at least one package or class segment, each segment starting with an uppercase or lowercase letter or an underscore and containing only letters, digits, underscores and dollar signs, with the segments joined by single dots; (3) the final segment is the method name and is followed immediately by a parenthesized location; (4) the location is either "Native Method", "Unknown Source", or a file name ending in .java followed by a colon and a line number of one or more digits, optionally followed by another colon and a column number of one or more digits; (5) nothing follows the closing parenthesis. The test is applied to a single line, so no anchors other than start and end of the string are needed, and the line must not be allowed to contain additional frames.

Match a log line that reports a duration greater than one second, expressed as a number followed by the unit "ms" (milliseconds). The number may be an integer or a decimal, and the value must be strictly above 1000.

We need to scan our application log for lines that contain a Python stack trace frame. A frame is a line that has the text "File" followed by a quoted file path, then the word "line", and then a number.
Match a log line that mentions a duration of more than one second, written as a number of seconds with the unit "s". The value may include a decimal part and must be greater than 1.

Match a log line that contains a duration greater than one second. The duration is written as an integer or decimal number followed by the unit "s" (seconds) or "sec" (seconds), with the number separated from the unit by an optional single space. items.description: We need to accept payments in Japanese yen from our international checkout. The amount field must accept a whole number of yen with no decimal part, and it can be written with comma-separated groups of three digits. The number must not start with a zero unless it's just the single digit zero. The field may optionally end with the yen symbol or the word 'yen' (in any case). Only the format is checked; no conversion or rounding is done.
Match a US dollar amount. It can be written with or without cents, and the dollar sign is required at the beginning.
Match a US dollar amount. The dollar sign is required, and the amount can be a whole number or have exactly two decimal places.

Our accounting system exports amounts with the three-letter currency code in front, like USD or EUR, followed by a space and then a number that can have an optional decimal part with up to two digits. We need to validate these strings; the code should be three uppercase letters, and the number part should be a whole number or have a dot and one or two digits. No thousands separators.

A valid euro price in French format must satisfy all of the following:
- The amount is a non-negative number, written with a comma as the decimal separator and an optional decimal part of exactly two digits.
- The integer part may be grouped with spaces (non-breaking or regular) every three digits, but the first group must not have a leading zero unless the entire integer part is a single zero.
- The price must end with the euro sign (€), optionally preceded by a space.
- No currency code is used.
Examples of valid inputs: "1 234,56 €", "0,99 €", "1234,56€". Invalid: "1.234,56 €", "1 234.56 €", "1234,5 €", "1234,56 $".

content:
{"items": [{"slot": 1, "description": "We store how long a job runs in a plain ISO 8601 duration format for our reporting exports. Only the shape and the month/day ranges are checked, not whether the date actually exists on a calendar.", "regex": "/^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$/"}, {"slot": 3, "description": "Our scheduler imports maintenance windows given as ISO 8601 durations, and the import rejects anything that is not a real duration: at least one component must be present after the P, components must appear in the order years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds, each number must be a whole number of one or more digits, the date part before T is optional and the time part after T is optional, but a bare P with nothing, a P with only a T, or a component out of order must all be refused. Fractional values are not used by our partners.", "regex": "/^P(?=\d|T\d)(?:\d+Y)?(?:\d+M)?(?:\d+D)?(?:T(?=\d)(?:\d+H)?(?:\d+M)?(?:\d+S)?)?$/"}, {"slot": 4, "description": "Validate the date-of-birth field, which is entered as a European date with day, month and year separated by slashes: dd/mm/yyyy. - Exactly four digits for the year.
- The separators must be forward slashes, nothing else.
- No surrounding whitespace is allowed.
- Only the format and the day/month ranges are checked; whether the day exists in that month (for example 31/02) is not verified.", "regex": "/^(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])\/(0[1-9]|1[0-2])\/\d{4}$/"}, {"slot": 5, "description": "Match an ISO 8601 timestamp with a timezone: date as yyyy-mm-dd, the letter T, time as hh:mm:ss with hours 00-23, minutes and seconds 00-59, and a timezone that is either the letter Z or an offset like +hh:mm or -hh:mm where the offset hours are 00-23 and the offset minutes are 00-59.", "regex": "/^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])T([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d(?:Z|[+-](?:[01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d)$/"}]}

items.description: We store how long a job runs in a plain ISO 8601 duration format for our reporting exports. The field only ever holds a duration with a day part and an hour part, like a number of days followed by a number of hours, both present and in that order, with the day count being one or more digits and the hour count being two digits. No other components and no fractional values are accepted.

Match an ISO 8601 calendar date in the extended format: four-digit year, hyphen, two-digit month from 01 to 12, hyphen, two-digit day from 01 to 31. Only the shape and the month/day ranges are checked, not whether the date actually exists on a calendar.

Our scheduler imports maintenance windows given as ISO 8601 durations, and the import rejects anything that is not a real duration: at least one component must be present after the P, components must appear in the order years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds, each number must be a whole number of one or more digits, the date part before T is optional and the time part after T is optional, but a bare P with nothing, a P with only a T, or a component out of order must all be refused. Fractional values are not used by our partners.

Validate the date-of-birth field, which is entered as a European date with day, month and year separated by slashes: dd/mm/yyyy. Rules:
- Exactly two digits for the day, 01 to 31.
- Exactly two digits for the month, 01 to 12.
- Exactly four digits for the year.
- The separators must be forward slashes, nothing else.
- No surrounding whitespace is allowed.
- Only the format and the day/month ranges are checked; whether the day exists in that month (for example 31/02) is not verified.

Match an ISO 8601 timestamp with a timezone: date as yyyy-mm-dd, the letter T, time as hh:mm:ss with hours 00-23, minutes and seconds 00-59, and a timezone that is either the letter Z or an offset like +hh:mm or -hh:mm where the offset hours are 00-23 and the offset minutes are 00-59.

A calendar version string must have the format:

- A dot.

We need to check Python dependency version specifiers used in our internal requirements files. A version specifier consists of an operator (one of ==, !=, <=, >=, <, >, ~=) followed immediately by a version number. The version number is a series of one or more dot-separated numeric components, where each component is one or more digits (leading zeros are allowed). The entire string must match this pattern.

A semantic version string consists of exactly three non-negative integer components, each without leading zeros (except the single digit 0), separated by dots. Optionally, a pre-release identifier may follow, introduced by a hyphen. The pre-release identifier is a series of dot-separated alphanumeric identifiers, where an identifier can contain only ASCII letters and digits, and must not be empty. No build metadata is allowed.

A semantic version string must follow the SemVer 2.0.0 format: three dot-separated numeric components (major, minor, patch), each a non-negative integer without leading zeros. An optional pre-release part may follow, starting with a hyphen and containing dot-separated identifiers where each identifier can include alphanumeric characters and hyphens, but cannot be empty. An optional build metadata part may follow, starting with a plus sign and containing dot-separated identifiers with the same allowed characters.
