An optional port number (digits only) may follow after a colon.

A URL path that starts with a forward slash, followed by one or more path segments. Each segment consists of letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, dots, or percent-encoded characters, and segments are separated by forward slashes. The path must not contain a question mark, so no query string is included. It may optionally end with a trailing slash.

items.description: A log line is valid if it contains a duration token indicating a time greater than 1 second. A duration token has the form <number><unit>, where <number> is one or more digits, optionally followed by a decimal part consisting of a dot and one or more digits. The unit must be one of: s, sec, second, ms (for milliseconds). For s, sec, and second units, the numeric value must be strictly greater than 1. For ms, the numeric value must be strictly greater than 1000. The duration token may appear anywhere in the line. A line may contain at most one duration token; if more than one is present, the line is invalid. The rest of the line must consist of one or more characters (any character except newline).

Our server logs occasionally include error codes formatted as ERR- followed by exactly three digits, and we need to identify log lines that contain at least one such error code. A line is valid if it includes the substring ERR- followed immediately by three digits (0-9). The error code can appear anywhere in the line. Lines that contain multiple error codes are also valid.

In our logging system, each log line must start with a severity level indicator: one of DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, or ERROR, in uppercase. After the level, there must be at least one space, but no other characters are allowed immediately after the level. The rest of the line can be any sequence of characters. A line is valid if it begins with one of these levels followed by one or more spaces and then any content.

Match an HTTP status line that starts with HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/1.0 followed by a space, then a three-digit status code that is in the 4xx or 5xx range (i.e., starts with 4 or 5). The line may optionally have a reason phrase after the status code, separated by a space. The status code must be exactly three digits.

Match a log line that begins with an ISO 8601 timestamp in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS followed by a space, then any text. The date part must be four digits, hyphen, two digits, hyphen, two digits. The time part must be two digits, colon, two digits, colon, two digits. There is no timezone indicator. The timestamp is followed by a single space and then any characters except newline.

items.description: A log line that mentions a duration greater than one second. The duration must be expressed in seconds and must be greater than 1.0 (i.e., not equal to or less than 1.0). The duration can be written as an integer or a decimal number, but if it is an integer it must be at least 2. The word 'seconds' must follow the number, separated by a space. The log line can have any content before and after this duration mention, but the duration must appear as a standalone token: the number and the word 'seconds' must be preceded by a word boundary and followed by a word boundary or end of string. The number must not have leading zeros unless it is exactly '0'. For example, '1.1 seconds' is valid, '2 seconds' is valid, but '1.0 seconds' is not, and '0.9 seconds' is not.

Our monitoring dashboard needs to flag server errors from access logs. The log lines look like a standard HTTP response status line: they start with the protocol version (either HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1), followed by a space, then a three-digit status code, then a space, and then a reason phrase that can contain any printable ASCII characters except newline. Only status lines where the status code is in the 400-599 range should be flagged. The protocol version must be exactly HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1 (all caps), and there must be exactly one space between the protocol, the status code, and the reason phrase. The reason phrase can be empty? No, it must be at least one character. The line must not contain any other characters before or after.

We need to automatically detect stack trace frames in our application logs to help with debugging. A stack trace frame is typically a line that contains a function name, followed by an optional file path and line number, but we only care about frames that include both a file path and a line number. The line must contain a pattern like 'at functionName (filePath:lineNumber)' or 'at filePath:lineNumber'. However, we only want to match lines that include a line number and a file path, and the file path must end with a file extension (like .js, .ts, .java, etc.) and the line number must be a positive integer. The line can have any text before and after, but the pattern must appear. Also, the function name may contain spaces and dots, but must not contain parentheses. The file path may contain slashes, dots, and alphanumeric characters, but not spaces. The entire pattern must be anchored to be the whole line? No, it's just a line containing this pattern. But we want to avoid false positives where the pattern is part of a larger word. So we require word boundaries around the 'at' and the pattern. The line may start with whitespace.

Match log lines that start with a log level. The log level must be one of the following uppercase words: DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, or FATAL. After the level, there must be exactly one space, and then the rest of the line can be any characters except newline. The log level must be at the very beginning of the line, and there should be no leading whitespace before it. The entire line must match from start to end.

In our performance reports, we need to extract log lines that indicate a response time greater than one second. The response time is always logged as a duration in seconds, written as a number followed by the unit 's' (for seconds), for example '1.5s' or '2s'. We consider a duration greater than one second if the numeric part is strictly greater than 1.0. The duration may be an integer or a decimal, but it must be greater than 1.0. It can appear anywhere in the line. The number must not have leading zeros. The duration is followed immediately by 's', with no space. The number and 's' must be preceded by a word boundary and followed by a word boundary. The line can contain any other text before and after, but the duration must appear as a standalone token. For example, '1.05s' is valid, '2.0s' is valid, but '1.0s' is not, and '0.99s' is not.

items.description:
A URL is valid if it meets all of the following:
- Starts with either "http://" or "https://" (case-sensitive).
- After the scheme, contains a host consisting of one or more labels separated by dots. Each label must start and end with a letter (a-z or A-Z) or a digit (0-9), and may contain hyphens in between. Labels are separated by single dots. The last label (top-level domain) must be at least two characters long and consist only of letters.
- After the host, an optional port may appear as a colon followed by one to five digits.
- After the host and optional port, an optional path may appear. If present, it must start with a slash and may be followed by any characters except spaces, newlines, and the characters ?, #, and control characters (code points below U+0020).
- The string must not contain any spaces, newlines, or other control characters anywhere.
- The string must not be followed by any other characters (i.e., the entire input must match).
Note: Query strings and fragments are not allowed; the path must not contain '?' or '#'.

Our design system stores brand colors as CSS hex codes. We need to validate that a string is a valid CSS hex color. Accept both the short form (3 hexadecimal digits) and the long form (6 hexadecimal digits), optionally prefixed with a hash symbol. The letters in the hex digits may be uppercase or lowercase. The entire string must be exactly the color code with no extra characters. For example, the string must consist of an optional '#', followed by either 3 or 6 characters from 0-9, A-F, a-f. No other characters are allowed.

Match a domain name that must end with the .co.uk top-level domain. The domain can have one or more labels before the .co.uk part. Each label must start with a letter or a digit, can contain letters, digits, and hyphens, but cannot start or end with a hyphen. The entire string must be a valid domain, with no spaces or other characters. The match should be case-insensitive.

Validate a CSS length value according to the CSS specification. A valid CSS length consists of an optional sign (plus or minus), followed by either an integer or a decimal number (with at least one digit before or after the decimal point, but not both missing), followed immediately by a unit. The unit must be one of the following, case-insensitive: px, em, rem, vh, vw, vmin, vmax, ex, ch, cm, mm, in, pt, pc, or q. items.description:
A valid branch name for our Git workflow must satisfy all of the following:
1. Start with one of the type prefixes `feature/`, `bugfix/`, `hotfix/`, or `release/` (lowercase, exactly these).
2. After the prefix, the rest of the name is one or more segments separated by forward slashes; each segment must be non-empty and consist only of lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens.
3. No segment may start or end with a dot, underscore, or hyphen.
4. Consecutive dots, underscores, or hyphens are not allowed within a segment.
5. The total branch name is at most 80 characters.

We need to validate container image references from the deployment form. Each reference is a repository path optionally followed by a tag. A repository path is one or more lowercase alphanumeric path components separated by forward slashes; each component may additionally contain dots, underscores, or hyphens but must begin and end with an alphanumeric character. If a tag is provided it is introduced by a colon and is up to 128 characters of ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots, or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. Tags are matched case-insensitively, repository paths are lowercase only.

Match a five-field cron expression. The fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, separated by single spaces. Minute and hour accept an asterisk, a single number, or a comma-separated list of numbers within their ranges (minute 0-59, hour 0-23). Day of month accepts an asterisk or a number from 1 to 31. Month accepts an asterisk or a number from 1 to 12. Day of week accepts an asterisk or a number from 0 to 7. No step or range syntax is allowed.
docker image ref optional :tag, lowercase repo, tag letters digits . _ - up to 128, starts alnum

Our CI pipeline needs to check the image field users type into the deploy dialog. An image is a repository path with optional tag, like on Docker Hub: repository components are lowercase letters and digits, may contain single dots, underscores or hyphens as inner separators, but a component can never start or end with one of those. Components are joined with slashes. The tag after the colon can be up to 128 characters made of letters, digits, underscores, dots and hyphens and must start with a letter or a digit. Reject anything with uppercase letters in the repository part or with multiple separators in a row.

The content between the quotes must be at least one character and must not contain the quote character that opened it.

The marketing team's ad headline field is limited by our banner layout: it can hold at most five words. A word is a run of non-whitespace characters separated from the next word by one or more spaces, tabs, or newlines. A file size consists of a positive number (integer or decimal) followed by exactly one space and one of these units: B, KB, MB, GB, TB. The unit may be written in uppercase or lowercase, but the whole unit must be consistent (e.g., 'KB' or 'kb', not 'Kb'). The number may have an optional decimal part with up to two digits.

A longitude in decimal degrees is a number between -180 and 180 inclusive. It may be an integer or have a fractional part, and may be preceded by an optional plus or minus sign. No other characters are allowed.

Coordinates in degrees, minutes and seconds are written as three non-negative integer components separated by the symbols °, ′, ″ (degree, prime, double prime). Degrees must be between 0 and 180 inclusive. Minutes and seconds must be between 0 and 59 inclusive. Both minutes and seconds must be exactly two digits. The value must be immediately followed by a hemisphere letter (N, S, E, W) in uppercase, with no space before it. The degrees part may have leading zeros. Only the format is checked, not geographic validity beyond the ranges.

items.description:
A string represents a monetary amount in Japanese yen. Format rules:
- May optionally begin with a yen sign (¥). If present, it must be followed by at least one digit.
- Then, groups of three digits separated by commas, with the first group containing one to three digits. No leading zeros unless the amount is zero itself.
- No decimal part or cents.
- The string must consist only of these characters, with no spaces or other symbols.
- The amount must be a valid non-negative integer (but the format only checks the pattern, not the numeric value).
A US dollar amount, optionally with cents. The dollar sign is required. Cents are optional and if present must be two digits.

We need to validate the price field in our e-commerce checkout. Prices must be non-negative and have exactly two decimal places, with a thousands separator using commas for amounts of 1,000 or more. No currency symbol is allowed. Use a period as the decimal separator. Leading zeros are not permitted unless the amount is 0.00. The maximum allowed value is 999,999.99. Spaces are not allowed.
Matches a Japanese yen amount without decimals, optionally preceded by a yen sign.

For our accounting export, we need to check that a monetary amount is formatted as a negative value using parentheses. The amount must have a thousands separator (comma) and exactly two decimal places, with a period as the decimal separator. The format is: an opening parenthesis, the amount, and a closing parenthesis, with no spaces. The amount must be at least 0.01 and at most 999,999,999.99. Leading zeros are not allowed except for amounts less than 1. No positive numbers or other characters are allowed.

The element part (preceded by __) and the modifier part (preceded by --) are both optional, but if the modifier is present, the element must also be present. No other characters are allowed. Rules: The string may contain one or more lines separated by newline characters (\n). Each line must not end with a space or tab character; however, a line may consist entirely of spaces or tabs without any non-whitespace characters, as long as it does not have trailing whitespace relative to its last non-whitespace character? Actually, the rule is: no line may end with a space or tab. This implies that if a line consists only of spaces/tabs, it would end with a space/tab, so such lines are invalid. However, an empty line (zero length) is allowed. The string as a whole must not end with a space or tab either, unless followed by a newline? Wait: the last line also must not end with space or tab. The newline characters themselves are not considered trailing whitespace; they are line terminators. So the pattern must ensure that every line (including the last) does not end with [ \t]. Lines are separated by \n. The regex must match the entire string from start to end. Also note that the string could be empty? Typically empty string is considered valid because it has no lines with trailing whitespace. The description should not mention regex syntax.

Validate a North American (NANP) phone number written in a national format. Rules:
1. The number consists of a three-digit area code, a three-digit central office code, and a four-digit subscriber number.
2. The area code must start with a digit from 2 to 9.
3. The central office code must start with a digit from 2 to 9.
4. Formatting is flexible: any of the following separators may appear—nothing (ten consecutive digits), a single space, a single hyphen, or a single dot—either between every group or only between some groups; the delimiter used before the central office code and the delimiter used before the subscriber number may differ, and either one may be absent. When a delimiter is present it must be exactly one character.
5. An optional leading '1' followed by a single space or hyphen may precede the area code.
6. No other characters, leading or trailing whitespace, or parentheses are permitted.

A North American phone number may be entered with or without a leading country code of 1, and an extension may follow. Accept ten digits with a first digit of 2 to 9 in both the area code and the exchange code. Grouping is free-form: a separator (space, hyphen, dot, or opening and closing parentheses around the area code) may appear between the area code and the exchange code and between the exchange code and the line number, and the two separators need not match. After the line number, the optional extension begins with an x, X, or the word ext (any capitalization, followed by a period if desired), then optional whitespace and one to five digits. Nothing else may surround the number.

Only the shape is verified, not whether the country code exists.

For our support portal, we accept phone numbers from customers around the world. A number may be entered with an international dialing prefix (a plus sign followed by one to three digits for the country code) or without one, in which case it is a local number of seven to fifteen digits. In either case the digits may be grouped using single spaces, hyphens, or dots as long as at least the first two digits of the actual number are present. Anything containing letters or parentheses must be rejected.

Log lines must begin with an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC, exactly in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ, where YYYY is four digits, MM is 01-12, DD is 01-31, HH is 00-23, mm is 00-59, ss is 00-59, followed by a literal 'Z'. Only the format is checked; leap years and invalid dates like February 30 are not validated beyond the numeric ranges given.

We need to validate duration strings in ISO 8601 format, such as P3DT4H, for our project management system. The duration should start with 'P', followed by optional components: years, months, days (each an integer followed by Y, M, or D respectively), and optionally a time part starting with 'T' containing hours, minutes, and seconds (each an integer followed by H, M, or S respectively). items.description:
A UK mobile number in national format.
- Starts with 07, followed by exactly nine digits.
- When written in international format it starts with +44 7, with no leading zero after the country code, followed by exactly nine digits.
- In the international form, a space is allowed between the country code and the subscriber number (i.e. after 7), but no other spaces or separators are allowed anywhere.
- Spaces in the national form are not allowed.

A North American Numbering Plan phone number: an optional leading 1 followed by a three-digit area code, a three-digit central office code, and a four-digit line number. The following separators are allowed between the groups: a hyphen, a dot, or a single space (the separator style may differ between the two gaps, but the same style may also be repeated). Separators are required if the leading 1 is present. Also allow the completely unseparated ten-digit form (no leading 1).

We're rolling out a checkout for our German storefront and the phone field has to accept the local number people actually type, with or without the +49 prefix. German numbers are written as a leading zero followed by between seven and eleven digits, so that's eight to twelve digits in total; when the +49 prefix is present the leading zero is dropped and the subscriber part stays seven to eleven digits. Let people put single spaces between the digits if they want, but nothing else.

For the French signup flow, the phone field must accept only French mobile numbers. In local form they begin with 06 or 07 followed by eight digits; in international form they begin with +33 followed by 6 or 7 and eight digits, with no leading zero. Single spaces are tolerated between digit groups in the local form only.

Accept a phone number that may or may not start with an international country code written as a plus sign immediately followed by one to three digits, which must be separated from the rest of the number by a single space; the remaining national part is a run of five to twelve digits in which single spaces may appear between digits. When no country code is given, the number must simply be that run of five to twelve digits. No other characters are permitted.

test file such as *.spec.ts or *.test.js
hidden dotfile name

items.description:
A valid Windows path with a drive letter must satisfy the following:
1. Start with a single uppercase or lowercase ASCII letter (A–Z, a–z).
2. Immediately follow the letter with a colon.
3. Then a backslash.
4. Then a non-empty sequence of one or more path segments separated by backslashes.
5. Each segment must consist of one or more characters from the set of ASCII letters, digits, underscore, hyphen, period, or space.
6. No segment may be empty.
7. The path must not end with a trailing backslash.

A test file name is a file name that ends with either .spec.ts or .test.js. The part before the extension must be a non-empty string of one or more characters that are not path separators or the null character. The file name must not contain any slash (/ or \) anywhere.

A hidden dotfile name must satisfy:
- It starts with a single dot.
- The first character after the dot is not a dot.
- The remaining part after the first character may contain any characters except path separators (/ or \) and the null character.
- The entire name must be non-empty after the leading dot.

A valid file name:
- Must be non-empty.
- Must not contain any of the following characters: /, \, :, *, ?, ", <, >, |.
- Must not contain control characters (ASCII 0–31).
- Must not end with a period or a space.
- Must not consist solely of periods or spaces.
- Must not be a reserved Windows device name (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1–COM9, LPT1–LPT9), case-insensitive, optionally followed by an extension.

items.description: We need to validate the mobile phone number field in our UK signup form. Only UK mobile numbers are accepted. The format should be either national or international, but not both mixed. National format must start with 07, followed by exactly 9 digits, and may optionally include spaces between digit groups. International format must start with +44, followed by the national number without the leading 0, i.e., 7 followed by 9 digits, and may optionally include spaces. No other characters are allowed except spaces as separators.

The input must be a North American phone number. It must consist of a 3-digit area code, a 3-digit central office code, and a 4-digit line number, in that order. The area code and central office code cannot start with 0 or 1. The number may be formatted with optional separators: a hyphen, a space, or a dot between the area code and central office code, and between the central office code and line number. The separators must be consistent: if a hyphen is used between the first two groups, a hyphen must also be used between the last two groups; similarly for space or dot. Alternatively, no separators may be used at all. The number may optionally be preceded by '1' followed by a space or hyphen, or no separator before the area code. The number may optionally be enclosed in parentheses around the area code, but if parentheses are used, the area code must be immediately followed by a space or hyphen, and the rest of the number must follow the separator consistency rule for the remaining groups.

Match a phone number that may optionally start with a country code. The country code, if present, is a plus sign followed by one to three digits. After the optional country code, there must be a sequence of digits, optionally grouped by spaces or hyphens. The total number of digits (excluding the country code) must be between 6 and 14. The groups can be of any length but must be separated by a single space or hyphen, and the string cannot start or end with a separator. If a country code is present, it must be directly followed by a digit or a space/hyphen then a digit.

We need to validate international phone numbers for our global SMS service. The number may optionally start with a plus sign followed by a country code (1 to 3 digits). After that, the national number should be 7 to 12 digits, possibly with spaces for readability. Spaces can appear between any digits but not at the beginning or end. The total number of digits (including country code if present) must be between 8 and 15. Also, if a plus sign is present, it must be immediately followed by a digit.

Validate a French mobile phone number. It must be exactly 10 digits, starting with 0, then 6 or 7, followed by 8 digits. Spaces are allowed between pairs of digits (e.g., after the second, fourth, sixth, and eighth digits), but not at the beginning or end, and not more than one space in a row.

- The line may have leading whitespace, including tabs or spaces, but at least one character of the line must be non-whitespace.
- After optional leading whitespace, the frame starts with "at " (lowercase a, lowercase t, single space).
- The qualified method or class name follows: one or more segments separated by dots. Each segment must start with a letter, underscore, or dollar sign, and may contain letters, digits, underscores, or dollar signs. There must be at least two segments (e.g., a class and a method).
- After the qualified name, the frame must include a source location in parentheses: a file name that ends with ".java" followed by a colon and a positive line number (no leading zeros except the single digit 0 is not allowed; line number starts with 1-9 and may be followed by digits).
- The line may have trailing whitespace after the closing parenthesis, and may have any characters before the leading whitespace? No, the frame is the only content, optionally surrounded by whitespace.

The frame may be preceded and followed by any other text on the line, but it must be present exactly in that form.

No, the line must start exactly with the level word.

The class/method path uses dot-separated identifiers, each starting with a letter, underscore, or dollar sign. The source location is a file name ending in ".java" followed by a colon and a line number (positive integer, no leading zeros). The line may end with whitespace.

items.description:
Validate a camelCase identifier for a TypeScript codebase. Rules:
- Must start with a lowercase ASCII letter (a-z).
- Every subsequent character is either a lowercase ASCII letter (a-z) or a digit (0-9), or an uppercase ASCII letter (A-Z) that begins a new word segment.
- An uppercase letter must be immediately followed by a lowercase letter, or by a digit that is itself followed by a lowercase letter (so acronyms and trailing digits on a segment are rejected).
- Never two uppercase letters in a row, and uppercase letters may not appear at the very end of the identifier.
- Digits may appear in the middle or at the end, but a digit may not be the first character.

We need to validate environment variable names used by our deployment tooling. An accepted name is written in all uppercase letters (A through Z) and digits and underscores only, must not start with a digit, and must not end with an underscore nor contain two underscores in a row.

Validate a CSS class name in kebab-case. Constraints:
1. The name is made of two or more lowercase alphanumeric words separated by single hyphens.
2. Each word must start with a lowercase letter a-z.
3. A word may contain digits after its first letter, but a word must not consist only of digits.
4. No leading hyphen, no trailing hyphen, and no consecutive hyphens.
5. The whole name must be at least 3 characters long.

Our internal editor plugin lets users type a variable name into a field, and before we hand it to the JavaScript engine we want to know it can legally be an identifier rather than throwing a syntax error. Only names that JavaScript would accept as a plain identifier should pass, and reserved words are fine since we are not checking semantics.

We read configuration from the process environment, so we need to reject any variable name the shell would not export. A valid name is all uppercase letters, digits, or underscores, and it has to begin with a letter or an underscore.

items.description:
A string is a valid semantic version (semver 2.0.0) if it consists of:
- a major version: a non-negative integer without leading zeros,
- a dot,
- a minor version: a non-negative integer without leading zeros,
- a dot,
- a patch version: a non-negative integer without leading zeros,
- optionally, a pre-release part introduced by a hyphen; the pre-release part is one or more dot-separated identifiers, where each identifier is either a non-empty sequence of alphanumeric characters (ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens) that must not consist solely of digits, or a numeric identifier (digits only) that must not have leading zeros,
- optionally, a build metadata part introduced by a plus sign; the build metadata part is one or more dot-separated identifiers, where each identifier is a non-empty sequence of alphanumeric characters (ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens).
Leading zeros are not allowed in major, minor, or patch versions.

Our build system accepts package dependencies on Python packages. A dependency specifies a package name optionally followed by a version constraint. The version constraint can be one of these operators: ==, !=, >=, <=, >, <, ~=, followed by a version number. The version number is a sequence of one or more dot-separated non-negative integers (no leading zeros unless the integer is exactly 0), optionally followed by a pre-release segment starting with a hyphen and consisting of dot-separated identifiers; each identifier can be alphanumeric (letters, digits) or a hyphen. There can be an optional space between the operator and the version. If no operator is given, just the package name is allowed. The package name is one or more ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, or dots, but it must not start with a hyphen, underscore, or dot. The entire string must match this format.

items.description:
Validate an npm package name. Rules:
- Total length must be between 1 and 214 characters.
- May start with an optional scope: an @ followed by a scope name of 1–214 characters, then a forward slash.
- The package name part must be 1–214 characters.
- Allowed characters are lowercase letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, and period.
- Must not start with a period or underscore.
- Must not contain uppercase letters, spaces, or any other characters.
- The scope name, if present, must not be empty and must not start with a period or underscore.

We want to enforce our semantic pull request title convention in CI. A valid title must start with a ticket key in square brackets, like a project code of 2 to 6 uppercase letters, a hyphen, and 1 to 5 digits. After the key and a single space, the title must begin with one of the allowed types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. The type must be followed by a colon, a space, and a non-empty description. The description can contain any characters except line breaks.
npm package name, scoped or not, lowercase, digits, hyphens, underscores, periods allowed, no leading period or underscore.

Match a Docker image reference. It may optionally start with a registry hostname (like registry.example.com:5000) followed by a slash. The repository path can contain one or more slash-separated components; each component must start and end with a lowercase letter or digit, and may contain periods, underscores, or double hyphens in between. After the repository, an optional tag may be specified with a colon followed by a tag name that starts with a word character and continues with word characters, periods, or hyphens.

In our monorepo, we need to validate package names that are used in a private registry. A valid package name must not start with a dot or an underscore. It may be optionally scoped with an @ prefix followed by the scope name and a slash; the scope name must also not start with a dot or underscore. The total name and the scope name must each be between 1 and 214 characters. Only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and periods are allowed. Additionally, the package name must contain at least one letter or digit (it cannot be entirely dots, hyphens, underscores, or a mix of those without any alphanumeric character).

items.description: semantic version with optional pre-release and build metadata

A Python version specifier consists of an operator followed by a version number. The operator can be one of ==, !=, <=, >=, <, >, ~=, or ===. The version number is a dot-separated list of numeric components, optionally followed by a pre-release segment and/or a local version segment. The pre-release segment starts with a hyphen and consists of dot-separated identifiers. The local version segment starts with a plus sign and consists of dot-separated identifiers. Identifiers are alphanumeric strings that may contain hyphens and underscores.

A semantic version string consists of three numeric components separated by periods: major, minor, and patch. Each component is a non-negative integer without leading zeros, except that the number zero itself is allowed. The version may optionally be followed by a pre-release segment that starts with a hyphen and consists of one or more dot-separated identifiers; each identifier may contain ASCII alphanumeric characters and hyphens, and numeric identifiers must not have leading zeros unless the identifier is just zero. The version may also optionally be followed by a build metadata segment that starts with a plus sign and consists of one or more dot-separated identifiers; each identifier may contain ASCII alphanumeric characters and hyphens, and numeric identifiers may have leading zeros. The pre-release and build metadata segments are independent: either, both, or neither may be present, but if both are present the pre-release must come first.

We store transaction amounts as text in our ledger export, and each amount must begin with a three-letter uppercase ISO 4217 currency code, then a single space, then the numeric value with no thousands separators, a dot as decimal separator, and exactly two decimal digits. Negative amounts are allowed and are written with a leading minus sign directly before the number, after the currency code and the space. No plus sign.

Specification for a currency amount token:
- Starts with a three-letter uppercase ISO 4217 currency code.
- Followed by exactly one space.
- Followed by the numeric value, which may be negative (leading minus sign, no plus sign).
- The integer part must not have leading zeros; it is either a single 0 or a nonzero digit followed by any digits.
- Optional fractional part: a dot followed by exactly two digits.
- Trailing spaces are not allowed.
- A space may optionally appear between the currency code and the number to improve readability, but if present, there must be exactly one space.
items.note: This slot's extra optional spacing makes it a distinct hard variant; pattern keeps a required single space for readability.

items.description: Negative amounts are written in accounting style: the number is wrapped in parentheses and there is no minus sign. Inside the parentheses the amount uses a dot decimal separator and may include commas as thousands separators, but only if every comma is followed by exactly three digits and the first group before the first comma has one to three digits with no leading zero unless the value is zero. Exactly two decimal digits are required after the dot. Positive amounts have no parentheses, no leading plus sign, and use the same thousands and decimal formatting.

Our checkout accepts prices in the catalog as plain numbers with exactly two decimal places. The price may be a whole number part with no thousands separators, or may be written with a leading zero for values under one. The integer part must not contain leading zeros unless it is a single zero. No currency symbol, no sign, no spaces.

- The amount uses a comma as the decimal separator and may include thousands separators (spaces) in groups of three digits, starting from the right of the integer part.
- The integer part must have at least one digit and must not start with a zero unless it is exactly zero.
- The fractional part, if present, must have exactly two digits.
- Thousands separators are optional; if present, they must be regular spaces (U+0020).
- Leading and trailing spaces are not allowed.
- No currency symbols other than € are permitted.

Examples of valid strings: "1 234,56 €", "0,99 €", "12 345 678,90 €".
Examples of invalid strings: "1234,56€", "1.234,56 €", "12,345.67 €", "1234,5 €", "1 234,56 €".

In our accounting ledger, negative amounts are written inside parentheses, like (123.45). We need a validation pattern for such negative amounts. The format should be: an opening parenthesis, then an optional dollar sign, then one or more digits, optionally followed by a decimal point and exactly two digits, then a closing parenthesis. No commas or spaces allowed. Positive amounts are handled elsewhere, so this pattern should only match the negative format described.

Match an amount in Japanese yen. The amount is written with digits only, no decimal part, and may include comma thousands separators. The string must end with the yen sign (¥). For example, ¥1000, ¥1,234,567, and ¥0 are valid, but ¥100.50, 1000¥, and ¥1,00 are not.

Validate a US dollar amount string.

Rules:
1. The string must start with a dollar sign ($).
2. The dollar sign is followed by an integer part with one or more digits.
3. The integer part may include commas as thousands separators. If commas are used, they must separate groups of exactly three digits, and the first group must have one to three digits. Leading zeros are allowed only as a single zero (e.g., "0" is valid, but "00" is not).
4. The integer part may be followed by an optional decimal part consisting of a dot and exactly two digits.
5. No other characters are allowed anywhere in the string.
6. The entire string must match from start to end.

Examples of valid strings: $1, $123, $1,234, $1,234.56, $0.99, $0, $1,000,000.00
Examples of invalid strings: $1,23, $1,234.5, $1.234, $1,234, $0123, $1,234.567

items.description: multiline text where no line ends with a space or tab

Our content editors paste article drafts into a text area, and the publishing pipeline chokes when any line ends with stray spaces or tabs. We need to reject a draft at validation time if any line has trailing whitespace, while allowing empty lines and all other content.

Validate a multi-line text block with these constraints:
1. The input may contain any characters including newline characters.
2. There must be at least one blank line, meaning two consecutive newline characters, or a newline at the very start or very end creating an empty line.
3. Empty input is not valid.

Specification for a multi-line short text field:
- The value must contain between one and three lines.
- Lines are separated by a single newline character (\n); a trailing newline is allowed and does not create a fourth line.
- Carriage returns (\r) are not permitted.
- Empty lines count as lines.

Users can enter notes in a multiline box, but every line must be free of trailing spaces or tabs; lines that are entirely empty are fine. Reject the whole entry if even one line ends with a space or tab character.

items.description: A percentage value from 0 to 100 inclusive, with up to two decimal places. The integer part must not have leading zeros unless it is exactly zero. A decimal point, if present, must be followed by one or two digits. The string must not contain any other characters.
An octet value, which is an integer between 0 and 255 inclusive. It must not have leading zeros unless the number is exactly zero.

A signed decimal number with an optional fractional part. 
- The number may start with an optional '+' or '-' sign.
- The integer part must consist of one or more digits, with no leading zeros unless the number is zero.
- A fractional part may follow, consisting of a decimal point and one or more digits.
- The entire string must be exactly this number; no other characters are allowed.

In our network configuration tool, users must provide a single octet value for each field. An octet is a whole number between 0 and 255, and leading zeros are not allowed unless the value is exactly 0.

In our physics simulation tool, users need to input numbers in scientific notation. The format is optional sign, a mantissa that is an integer or decimal with no leading zeros (unless zero), followed by 'e' or 'E', an optional sign, and an exponent of one or more digits with no leading zeros (unless zero). Examples of numbers: 1.23e4, -5E-10, 0.0e0. The entire input must match this format.

items.description: Our shipping form needs a weight field. Users must enter the weight as a number (which may have a decimal part) followed by either 'kg' or 'g'. The unit must be lowercase and directly attached to the number (no space). The number must be positive and cannot have leading zeros unless it is zero itself, but zero weights are not allowed. Only one optional decimal part is allowed.
Match a weight written as a number followed by either 'kg' or 'g'.

We need to validate weights in our inventory system. The format is either a whole number of kilograms, or a decimal number of kilograms with up to three decimal places, or a whole number of grams. The unit 'kg' or 'g' must be lowercase. The numeric part must not have leading zeros unless it is exactly zero (e.g., '0kg' is allowed). For a decimal kilogram value, the decimal part must be present and can have one to three digits. No spaces are allowed. For example, '1.5kg' is valid, but '1.5g' is not because grams must be whole numbers.

Our product feed requires screen resolutions in the format widthxheight. Both width and height must be whole numbers without leading zeros (unless the number is zero, but zero is not a valid dimension). The 'x' must be lowercase. No spaces around the 'x'.

A latitude coordinate is a decimal number between -90 and 90 inclusive. It must have an optional minus sign (for negative values), followed by an integer part from 0 to 90, and optionally a decimal part with exactly one to six digits after a dot. The integer part must not have leading zeros unless it is exactly zero (e.g., '0.123' is valid, but '00.123' is not). If the integer part is 90, the decimal part must be absent or all zeros (i.e., 90.0 is allowed but 90.1 is not). The decimal part, if present, must have at least one digit.

2. 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255.
3. 192.168.0.0 through 192.168.255.255.
4. Each octet is 0–255 with no leading zeros except the single digit 0.
5. The input is the complete address, nothing else.

3. The string must end with the euro sign € immediately after the decimal digits, with no space before the €.

A line is considered a failure if it begins with a protocol version token, followed by a space, then a three-digit status code where the first digit is 4 or 5, then a space and a reason phrase that may be empty. The protocol version is either 'HTTP/1.0' or 'HTTP/1.1'. The reason phrase must consist of zero or more printable ASCII characters (U+0020 to U+007E) and must not contain carriage return or newline. For 'ms', the value must be greater than 1000; for 's', greater than 1; for 'min', greater than 0. The line may contain any other characters before or after the duration, but the duration token must be a separate word delimited by non-word characters or string boundaries.

Our log aggregation pipeline expects every log entry to start with an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC, like '2023-04-05T12:34:56Z'. items.description: We need to validate the package name field when users publish to our private registry. It must accept either an unscoped name or a scoped name starting with @. An unscoped name must start with a lowercase letter, can contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, dots, and underscores, and must be at most 214 characters long. A scoped name consists of an @, then a scope part that follows the same character rules as an unscoped name (but may also start with a digit or hyphen? Actually npm scope must start with letter? The spec says scope must start with a letter? Let's define: scope part must be at least one character, start with a lowercase letter, and otherwise follow the same allowed characters as the unscoped name; then a slash, then a package part that follows the same rules as an unscoped name. The total length must be at most 214 characters. We are only checking the format, not whether the package actually exists.

A Docker image reference consists of an optional registry hostname, a repository path, and an optional tag. The registry hostname, if present, is a domain name (e.g., registry.example.com:5000) followed by a slash. The repository path is one or more path components separated by slashes; each component must start with a lowercase letter or digit, and may contain lowercase letters, digits, periods, underscores, and hyphens. The tag, if present, is a colon followed by one or more word characters (letters, digits, underscore), and is optional. The whole string must not contain uppercase letters.

A Conventional Commits title has the form: a type, an optional scope in parentheses, an optional exclamation mark to indicate a breaking change, then a colon and a space, followed by a description. The type must be one of the following words, in lowercase: build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test. The scope, if present, must be a non-empty string of characters that are not parentheses. The description must be non-empty and must not start or end with whitespace, but may contain any other characters. The entire title must be on a single line.

Our pull request titles must follow a semantic format with a ticket key. The title must start with an optional type prefix (feat, fix, chore, docs, style, refactor, perf, test) in lowercase, followed by a colon and a space. Then there must be a ticket key in square brackets, which is an uppercase project code of two or more letters, a hyphen, and a number (at least one digit). After the ticket key, there must be a space and then a non-empty description. The description may contain any characters except newlines. The ticket key and description are mandatory; the type prefix is optional. The whole title must be on one line.

In our CI pipeline we need to validate the image reference that developers put in their deployment config. The reference can optionally start with a registry hostname followed by a slash. The hostname must be a valid domain name (letters, digits, hyphens, periods) and may include a port number (colon followed by digits). After the optional registry, there is a repository path made of one or more components separated by slashes. Each component must start with a lowercase letter or digit, and can contain lowercase letters, digits, periods, underscores, and hyphens. Finally, an optional tag can be specified as a colon followed by one or more word characters. The whole string must not contain uppercase letters. We only need to check the format, not whether the image exists.

items.description:
Validate a UK mobile number. Rules:
- May optionally start with the international dialling prefix "+44" or the national trunk prefix "0".
- After the prefix, the number starts with 7 (all UK mobile ranges begin with 07).
- Exactly 9 more digits follow the leading 7, so 10 digits total after an optional "+44" or 11 digits when written with a leading 0.
- No spaces, hyphens or parentheses are permitted.

Match a phone number in E.164 format: a plus sign followed by a country code and subscriber number, where the first digit of the country code is 1 through 9 and the total number of digits is between 8 and 15 inclusive. No spaces or other separators are allowed.

Accept a national phone number of exactly 9 digits, optionally preceded by a country code written as a plus sign followed by 1 to 3 digits whose first digit is not zero. The country code may only be present in the plus-sign form; a bare national number contains just the 9 digits. No separators of any kind are allowed.

For our EU customer contact field we accept a phone number written with the national format of exactly 10 digits, or the same number written with an international country code. When the country code is supplied it is introduced by a plus sign and consists of one to three digits not starting with zero. Spaces and hyphens may be used freely as grouping separators anywhere in the number, but a number must never start or end with one of them.

The number field accepts either a local number of exactly eight digits, or that same eight-digit number preceded by an international country code, which is a plus sign followed by one to three digits with a nonzero first digit. Any grouping spaces are allowed only between digits: the string may not begin or end with a space, and two spaces may not appear consecutively.

Our mapping feature needs a latitude field. Users enter a decimal number between -90 and 90 inclusive. The number may have an optional minus sign, up to two digits before the decimal point (no leading zeros unless the integer part is exactly 0), and an optional fractional part with one or more digits. A decimal point is allowed only if followed by at least one digit. No plus sign or spaces.

The dimensions field must follow these rules:
- Format: <width>x<height>, where x is a lowercase letter.
- Width and height are positive integers without leading zeros (except the number 0 itself, but 0 is not allowed as a dimension).
- No spaces around the x or at the ends.
- The entire string must match.

A geographic coordinate in degrees, minutes and seconds must be provided as follows:
- Degrees: one to three digits, no leading zeros unless the value is 0 (but 0 is allowed as a single digit).
- Followed by the degree symbol °.
- Minutes: two digits from 00 to 59, including leading zero if needed.
- Followed by the prime symbol ′.
- Seconds: two digits from 00 to 59, including leading zero if needed.
- Followed by the double prime symbol ″.
- Finally, a hemisphere indicator: one of N, S, E, W (uppercase).
- No spaces between parts.

A weight can be given in kilograms or grams. It is written as a number, optionally with a decimal point and exactly two decimal places, followed by a space and then either kg or g (lowercase). items.description:
A Conventional Commits subject line consists of a type, an optional scope, an optional breaking-change marker, and a description, in that order.

1. The type must be one of: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. It is written in lowercase letters only.
2. The type may be followed by a scope: an opening parenthesis, then one or more lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, then a closing parenthesis.
3. After the type or scope, an exclamation mark may appear to mark a breaking change.
4. A colon and exactly one space separate the header from the description.
5. The description is one or more characters that are not line breaks. It must not be empty.

npm package names: lowercase only, optionally scoped as @scope/name; each part starts with a letter or digit and may contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and dots; total length at most 214 characters.

npm package name, scoped or unscoped: only lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores; must not start with a dot or underscore; a scope is @ followed by a name, then a slash, then the package name; the string must not end with a slash.

We need to validate the name our users give to a Kubernetes resource in the deploy form. It has to be a DNS label: lowercase alphanumeric characters or hyphens, must begin and end with an alphanumeric character, and be at most 63 characters long.

For our scheduler UI we accept a simplified five-field cron expression. The five whitespace-separated fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, in that order. Each field is either a single number, a range of two numbers separated by a hyphen, or a comma-separated list of those. Minutes run from 0 to 59, hours from 0 to 23, days of month from 1 to 31, months from 1 to 12, and days of week from 0 to 7. A star alone is accepted only as the whole field. Ranges must not be reversed.

items.description:
A Python version specifier string must be validated. The specifier consists of an optional series of version specifiers separated by commas and optional spaces. Each version specifier has:
- An operator, which is one of: ~=, ==, !=, <=, >=, <, >, or ===
- A version number that starts with an optional 'v' or 'V', followed by one or more digits, then optionally a dot and digits, then optionally a dot and digits, then optionally a dot and digits.
- An optional local version segment starting with '+' followed by alphanumeric characters and periods.
- An optional pre-release segment: a hyphen followed by alphanumeric characters and periods.
- An optional post-release segment: ".post" followed by digits.
- An optional development release: ".dev" followed by digits.
The entire specifier must match from start to end. Whitespace is allowed around commas and operators.

We need to validate the version string our build system outputs for package releases. The version must follow semantic versioning: major, minor, and patch numbers separated by dots, each being a non-negative integer without leading zeros. After the patch, there can be an optional pre-release label: a hyphen followed by one or more dot-separated identifiers, where each identifier is either a number without leading zeros or an alphanumeric string (letters, digits, hyphens). There can also be an optional build metadata part: a plus sign followed by one or more dot-separated identifiers, each consisting of alphanumeric characters (letters and digits) and hyphens. The pre-release and build metadata can appear independently or together, in that order.

A Python version specifier is a string that describes a range of allowed versions. It is a comma-separated list of one or more version constraints. Each constraint is an operator followed by a version number, where the operator is one of '~=', '==', '!=', '<=', '>=', '<', '>', or '==='. The version number may optionally start with 'v' or 'V', followed by one or more numeric parts separated by dots (each part is one or more digits), up to four parts. After the numeric parts, an optional pre-release (a hyphen followed by alphanumeric characters and periods) or a post-release ('.post' followed by digits) or a development release ('.dev' followed by digits) may appear. Commas separating constraints may have whitespace around them, and the entire specifier may have leading or trailing whitespace.

We need to check that version numbers in our app follow semantic versioning: a major, minor, and patch number separated by dots. Each number is a non-negative integer without leading zeros (unless it is exactly zero). No other characters are allowed.

Our system requires calendar version strings in the format year.month, where the year is exactly four digits, the month is two digits from 01 to 12, and they are separated by a dot. No other characters are allowed.

Our analytics dashboard needs to verify that the 'size' parameter coming from client-side code is a valid CSS length before using it to position elements. Units are one of: px, em, rem, %, vw, vh, vmin, vmax, cm, mm, in, pt, pc, ex, ch. Pull request titles must follow the semantic PR title format and include a ticket key. The title must consist of a type, an optional scope in parentheses, a colon and a space, followed by a description that contains a Jira ticket key in the form of two to four uppercase letters, a hyphen, and one to five digits. The type must be one of: build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test. The scope, if present, must be a sequence of one or more lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens. The description must contain at least one ticket key and may have other text before or after it. The entire title must be at most 120 characters.

In our deployment configuration, we need to validate the Docker image reference field. Users should enter a Docker image name, optionally with a tag. The image name must start with a lowercase letter or digit, and can contain lowercase letters, digits, periods, underscores, and hyphens. If a tag is provided, it must be separated by a colon and consist of one or more word characters (letters, digits, or underscores). The total length of the image name before the tag must not exceed 255 characters.

Match a Docker image reference that may optionally include a registry, repository, and tag. The reference can start with an optional registry hostname (which can include a port) followed by a slash. The repository part must consist of one or more path components separated by slashes, where each component must start and end with a lowercase letter or digit, and may contain periods, underscores, or hyphens in between. An optional tag can be appended after a colon, consisting of one or more word characters. The total length of the image name (excluding the tag) must not exceed 255 characters.

Validate an npm package name. It can be either unscoped or scoped. An unscoped name must be a lowercase alphanumeric string that may contain hyphens, underscores, and periods, but must not start with a period or underscore. A scoped name starts with an at sign, followed by a scope (same rules as unscoped name), a slash, and a package name (same rules as unscoped name). The total length must not exceed 214 characters.

items.description: Validate an HTTP status line as a string. The line must begin with 'HTTP/' followed by a version consisting of one or more digits, a dot, and one or more digits. Then a space, followed by exactly three digits (the status code). The status code must start with 4 or 5 (i.e., represent a 4xx or 5xx code). After the status code, a space, then a reason phrase of one or more characters (any except newline). No leading or trailing whitespace is allowed.

Our server writes log lines that always start with a severity level: one of the uppercase words ERROR, WARN, INFO, or DEBUG, immediately followed by a colon and a space. The rest of the line is a non-empty message that may contain any characters except newline. We need to check if a given log line matches this format exactly from beginning to end.

Match a single line from an Apache or nginx access log. The line starts with the client IP address: four dot-separated decimal numbers, each between 0 and 255, with no leading zeros unless the number is exactly 0. Then a space, a hyphen, a space, a hyphen, a space, and a timestamp enclosed in square brackets. The timestamp format is dd/MMM/yyyy:HH:mm:ss Z, where dd is two digits, MMM is the three-letter English month abbreviation (capitalized), yyyy is four digits, HH, mm, ss are two digits, and Z is a timezone offset like +0000 or -0700. After the timestamp and a closing bracket, a space, a double-quoted HTTP request line (e.g., "GET /index.html HTTP/1.1"), then a space, a three-digit status code, a space, and a size in bytes (one or more digits, or a hyphen if unknown). No extra spaces or characters are allowed before or after.

Match a log line that contains an error code anywhere in it. The error code consists of the uppercase letters 'ERR' followed by exactly three digits. The line must contain at least one such code, but the code may be preceded or followed by any other characters (including spaces, punctuation, etc.) except that the line cannot contain newline characters. The entire string is not required to be only the error code; we just need to know if any error code is present.

We receive access logs from our web servers and need to validate each line before storing it. The expected format is the common log format: an IP address (four dot-separated numbers, each 0-255), then a space, a hyphen, a space, a hyphen, a space, a date-time in square brackets in the format day/month/year:hour:minute:second zone, where day is two digits, month is two digits, year is four digits, hour, minute, second are two digits each, and zone is a plus or minus followed by four digits. After that, a space, a quoted HTTP request line (anything inside double quotes), a space, a three-digit status code, a space, and the response size in bytes (a number or a hyphen). No extra characters before or after.

1. Consists of lowercase alphanumeric characters, '-' or '.'.
2. Must start and end with an alphanumeric character.
3. Maximum length 253 characters.
4. Must not be a DNS subdomain? No, that's only for some resources; for generic resources use the DNS-1123 subdomain rules: lowercase alphanumeric, '-', '.', start/end alphanumeric, max 253. Use exactly these rules.

items.description: A Docker image reference must match the following rules: it consists of a registry hostname (optional, only when the reference includes a registry), a repository path, and an optional tag. The registry hostname, if present, is a domain name (one or more dot-separated labels, each label starting and ending with an alphanumeric character and allowing hyphens in the middle). The repository path is a sequence of one or more path components separated by forward slashes. Each path component must start and end with an alphanumeric character and may contain lowercase letters, digits, periods, underscores, and double underscores; single underscores and periods are also allowed. Tags are optional and, when present, must be separated from the repository by a colon and must start with a word character (letter, digit, or underscore) and may be followed by up to 127 word characters, periods, or hyphens. The entire reference must not exceed 255 characters. The check is only for format; existence or validity of the image is not verified.
conventional commit title

We need to enforce a standard naming scheme for branches in our new project repository so that our CI/CD pipeline can trigger correctly based on branch type. Branch names should begin with a type indicator from this list: feature, bugfix, hotfix, release, or chore, followed by a forward slash, then a short description. The short description must be all lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, with no consecutive hyphens and not starting or ending with a hyphen.

A semantic pull request title consists of a type, an optional scope, an optional breaking-change marker, and a subject, optionally preceded by a ticket key. Valid examples follow this structure: [TICKET-123] type(scope)!: subject. The ticket key is optional and, if present, is a sequence of uppercase letters, a hyphen, and digits, enclosed in square brackets, followed by a space. The type is one of feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, or revert. The scope is optional and, when present, appears in parentheses immediately after the type and must be lowercase alphanumeric words separated by hyphens. The breaking-change marker is an optional exclamation mark immediately after the scope (or type if no scope). A colon and a space must follow the type/scope/marker. The subject must contain at least one character and must not start or end with whitespace; it may contain any printable characters except newlines.

A simplified five-field cron expression must satisfy these constraints: the five fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, in that order, separated by single spaces. Minute: 0–59. Hour: 0–23. Day of month: 1–31. Month: 1–12. Day of week: 0–6, where 0 is Sunday. Each field accepts a single number, a comma-separated list of numbers, a range of two numbers separated by a hyphen (inclusive), a step value across a range or a wildcard (e.g., */n or a-b/n), or a wildcard (*). A step value is a forward slash followed by a positive integer no greater than the field's maximum. Ranges must be in ascending order and within the field's bounds. Lists must contain at least one item and items must not be empty. No field name or special macros are allowed. The entire expression must be exactly five fields.

items.description:
Write a regular expression for a semantic pull request title.

Rules:
- The title must start with a ticket key: an uppercase project code of 2 to 8 letters, followed by a hyphen, followed by 1 to 6 digits.
- After the ticket key there must be exactly one space.
- The rest of the title must be a non-empty semantic subject: it must begin with one of the conventional types `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, or `refactor`, followed immediately by `:` (no space before the colon), then exactly one space, then a non-empty body.
- The body may contain any characters except newline; it must not end with a space.

We let customers define simple recurring maintenance windows with a five-field cron expression, but we only support the basic pager syntax: each of the five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) may be either a number, a range, a comma-separated list of numbers and ranges, or a single asterisk. We do not support step values, names, question marks, or any other extensions. In each field the numbers must stay within their normal bounds: minute and hour use the usual 0–23 / 0–59 limits, day of month is 1–31, month is 1–12, and day of week is 0–6. Exactly five fields separated by single spaces are required, with no leading or trailing whitespace.

Validate a simplified five-field cron expression.

- The string must consist of exactly five fields separated by a single space.

- Day-of-month field: value range 1–31.
- Month field: value range 1–12.
- Day-of-week field: value range 0–6.
- No leading or trailing spaces, and no step values or names are allowed.

- Optional scope must be enclosed in parentheses and contain at least one character; allowed characters are letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, dot, and slash.

- The colon must be followed by exactly one space, then a non-empty description that does not contain newline characters.

- Unscoped: a single component.
- Scoped: starts with @, followed by a scope component, a forward slash, and a package component.
- Each component must be at least one character long, may contain lowercase letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, and dot.
- Components must not start with a dot or underscore.

The type must be one of: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert. The scope, if present, must be enclosed in parentheses and contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens; it cannot be empty. The breaking change indicator is an exclamation mark that appears immediately after the type or the closing parenthesis of the scope, but before the colon. The colon must be followed by exactly one space and a non-empty description. The description may contain any characters except newline. The entire string must be on one line.

items.description: Our dashboard ingests rotating service logs and the parser needs to tell whether each incoming line begins with a complete ISO 8601 UTC timestamp, rendered as four digits for the year, a hyphen, two digits for the month, a hyphen, two digits for the day, then a capital T, two digits for the hour, a colon, two digits for the minute, a colon, two digits for the second, and a trailing uppercase Z. Only the shape matters, not whether the date is real. After that timestamped prefix there must be a space and at least one more character of log text.

Validate a single combined access log line. Constraints:
1. The line starts with a client IP address written as four dot-separated decimal octets, each one to three digits, no leading zeros unless the octet is exactly 0, and each octet at most 255.
2. Then a space, an opening square bracket, a timestamp of exactly the form day/month/year:hour:minute:second with two-digit day, two-digit month, four-digit year and two-digit time components, a closing bracket, and a space.
3. Then the quoted request section: a double quote, an uppercase HTTP method of three to seven letters, a space, a request target that starts with a slash and contains no space or double quote, optionally a space followed by the literal HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1, then a closing double quote.
4. Then a space, a three-digit status code, a space, and the response size as at least one digit (a hyphen is not accepted).
5. The rest of the line, if anything, is free text.

Check whether a log line reports a duration of more than one second. A duration is written as a number immediately followed by a unit: ms for milliseconds, s for seconds, m for minutes, or h for hours. At least one such duration must appear anywhere in the line, and it counts as over one second when it is at least 1000 ms, at least 1 s, at least 1 m, or at least 1 h. Fractional values are allowed, but the whole part must contain no leading zeros unless the value is a bare 0 (for example 05 s is not valid input at all). A duration only counts if it is not glued to a letter, digit, dot, or underscore on either side.

Ops wants to flag slow requests from our text logs. A request line mentions a duration as a number followed immediately by a unit, one of ms, s, m or h, and we only care about the ones that took longer than a whole second, so anything in seconds over 1, or in minutes/hours, or in ms over 1000. We only look at lines whose duration string is standalone, not part of a longer word or version number.

Our release pipeline rejects pull request titles that are not linked to a ticket. The whole branch name must be at most 60 characters long.

items.description: A log line must start with an ISO 8601 timestamp in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS followed by a single space and then the log message. The timestamp uses UTC (Z) or a numeric offset like +02:00 or -05:30; the offset part is optional. The date and time separators are fixed as shown, with a 'T' between date and time. The message part can be any sequence of characters except newline. Validate the entire line from start to end.

Match a single Apache or nginx common log format line. It starts with the client IP address (IPv4 or IPv6), then a space, then a hyphen, then another space, then the remote logname (a hyphen if not available), then a space, then the authenticated user (a hyphen if not available), then a space, then a date enclosed in square brackets in the format day/month/year:hour:minute:second timezone, then a space, then a double-quoted request line that may contain any characters except newline, then a space, then a three-digit HTTP status code, then a space, then a non-negative integer number of bytes sent (or a hyphen if zero), and optionally additional fields after that.

A log line must begin with a severity level, exactly one of DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, or FATAL, written in uppercase. After the level, there must be a space, followed by the log message. The log message can be any non-empty sequence of characters, including spaces, but cannot contain newline characters. The entire string must be exactly one such line; no extra characters before or after.

We need to check log lines to find any that contain a stack trace frame, which looks like 'at functionName (file.ext:lineNumber)' or 'at file.ext:lineNumber'. The frame may appear anywhere in the line. The function name (if present) is a non-space sequence possibly containing dots or brackets, followed by a space, then the file path in parentheses that ends with a colon and one or more digits, or the file path directly after 'at' without parentheses but ending with a colon and digits. Specifically, after 'at ' we allow either: a sequence of non-whitespace characters (the function name) followed by ' (' and then a file path (any characters except newline and closing parenthesis) ending with ':<digits>)', or just a file path (any characters except newline and space) ending with ':<digits>'. Note that the function name might contain parentheses in rare cases, but we ignore that for simplicity. The line may have any content before or after the frame. For this check, we just need to know if the line contains such a frame.

A log line must start with a level label in the format [LEVEL] where LEVEL is one of TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR, or FATAL, exactly in uppercase, enclosed in square brackets. After the closing bracket, there must be a space and then the message. The message must not contain newline characters. The whole string must be a single log line, anchored from start to end.

items.description: apache or nginx combined access log line

We need to identify slow requests from our monitoring logs. A log line is considered slow if it explicitly mentions a duration greater than one second. The duration may appear as a plain number followed by 's' or 'sec', or as an integer number of milliseconds greater than 1000 followed by 'ms'. The line should be flagged only if it contains such a duration anywhere.
line with duration > 1s

Our performance dashboard shows response times. We need to filter log entries where the request took longer than one second. The duration must be explicitly mentioned in the log line as a number followed by a unit: either seconds (s or sec) or milliseconds (ms). Only durations greater than 1 second should be matched. Note that a bare number without a unit should not be considered.

The line contains a stack trace frame. A stack trace frame is a line that starts with optional whitespace, followed by the word 'at', then whitespace, then a JavaScript-style function name (possibly with a namespace like 'Object.<anonymous>' or 'new Foo'), a space, and then a location in parentheses (file path or URL, line, and column, separated by colons). The line must end after the closing parenthesis.

items.description: Our support team needs to quickly identify server errors from the access log. Each log entry starts with an HTTP status line in the common log format: a version token like HTTP/1.1, followed by a space, then exactly three digits. Only status codes in the 4xx or 5xx ranges indicate a server-side error and should be flagged. The line may be followed by other log fields, but the status line itself is at the beginning. We need a pattern that tests if the entire string is such a status line, so it must be exactly 'HTTP/' followed by a version number (one or more digits, a dot, one or more digits), a space, and a three-digit code starting with 4 or 5. No extra characters before or after.
log line containing an error code like ERR-404

Validate an HTTP status line in the format: 'HTTP/<major>.<minor> <status-code>'. The major and minor version numbers are one or more digits. The status code must be exactly three digits and must begin with '4' or '5'. The entire string must match this format exactly; no leading or trailing whitespace or other characters are allowed.

A log line is valid if it contains an error code consisting of the uppercase letters 'ERR' followed by a hyphen and one or more digits. The error code may appear anywhere within the line. The line may have any other characters before or after the error code. There is no requirement for the line to start or end with the error code.

We need to find log lines that mention a duration greater than one second. Durations appear as numbers followed by a unit: 's' for seconds, 'ms' for milliseconds, or 'min' for minutes (case-insensitive). The number may be an integer or decimal with a dot. The duration must be part of the line, but the line can have any other text around it. We only want to match if the numeric value is strictly greater than 1 second when converted to seconds (1 min = 60 s). For example, 1.5s, 1500ms, and 2min should match, but 1s, 1000ms, and 0.5min should not.

We use a git branch naming convention where each branch name consists of a type, a slash, a short description, and optionally a ticket key. The type must be one of: feature, bugfix, hotfix, release, or chore. Check that a log line begins with an ISO 8601 timestamp and a space. The timestamp must be in the exact format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ, using four digits for the year, two digits each for month, day, hour, minute, and second, the literal letter T, and the literal letter Z at the end.

Check if a log line mentions a duration that is more than one second. The duration must be written with one or more digits, followed by the letter s (for seconds), and can be anywhere in the line. The number part should not be preceded by a digit or a dot. For example, 1000s or 2s are more than one second, but 1s is not. Also allow optional decimal part, so 1.1s is valid and more than one second. The match should treat the duration as a standalone token, not part of a longer number like 1000ms or 1.5s.

A line is considered slow if it contains a duration in seconds, formatted as a decimal number with an 's' suffix, where the numeric value is greater than 1. The number may have an optional integer part and an optional fractional part, but must be positive. Leading zeros are not allowed in the integer part unless the integer part is exactly zero. The value must be greater than 1.0. The duration can appear anywhere in the line, but must not be part of a larger word (i.e., it must be preceded by start-of-line, whitespace, or an opening punctuation like '(', '[', '{', '<', and followed by 's' and then whitespace or end-of-line).
