A Conventional Commits subject line consists of a type, an optional scope, an optional breaking-change marker, then a colon and a space, then a non-empty description.
- Type: one of feat, fix, build, chore, ci, docs, style, refactor, perf, test.
- Scope: optional, written as a parenthesised sequence of one or more lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens.
- Breaking marker: optional single exclamation mark placed after the type or after the scope.
- Then a colon, exactly one space, and the description, which is one or more characters and must not contain a line break.
Only the header line is checked; any body or footer is out of scope.
five-field cron expression simplified

Match an npm package name. It is either a plain name or a scoped name starting with an at-sign, a scope, and a slash. Every segment consists of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, or dots, must start with a letter or digit, and is at most 214 characters long.

A Kubernetes resource name is a DNS subdomain: lowercase alphanumeric characters, hyphens, and dots, with each dot-separated label starting and ending with an alphanumeric character. The whole name is at most 253 characters, and no label may exceed 63 characters.

Validate a Conventional Commits header:
1. It begins with a type keyword from the set feat, fix, build, chore, ci, docs, style, refactor, perf, test.
2. An optional scope may follow in parentheses; the scope is one or more characters from lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
3. An optional exclamation mark may follow the type or the closing parenthesis to denote a breaking change.
4. A colon and a single space must follow.
5. The description is one or more characters, and must not contain a carriage return or line feed.
Entries missing the space after the colon, using an unknown type, or containing an empty description are invalid.

- The line begins with either HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/1.0 (the version token), followed by a single space.
- Then a three-digit status code.
- The code must be in the 4xx or 5xx class: first digit 4 or 5, followed by two digits.
- A single space must follow the code, then a reason phrase.
- The reason phrase is one or more printable ASCII characters (U+0020 to U+007E), including spaces; it cannot be empty.
- No leading or trailing whitespace beyond what is described.

Our support team triages incoming server output and needs to pull out any line that signals a failure of the payment gateway. The gateway always stamps its failures with a code in the form PG- followed by exactly three digits, and those lines are the only ones we care about. We need to know whether a given log line contains such a marker anywhere in it, regardless of what comes before or after.

line containing ERR-12345 style code anywhere
A log line begins with the severity level WARN followed by a space, with any text allowed after that.

items.description: Our content moderation system needs to enforce a strict limit on the length of user-submitted notes. We accept a note only if it consists of one, two, or three lines. Each line is separated by a newline character, and no line may contain another newline. The entire note may be empty or consist of up to three lines, where each line can contain any characters. However, the note must not contain more than two newline characters (so at most three lines). This is for a text field where users can write short remarks; we need to validate that the input does not exceed three lines before saving.

The string must contain at least one blank line, meaning two consecutive newline characters with nothing between them, or a newline followed by only whitespace and another newline? Actually, define as two newline characters adjacent, i.e., an empty line. Also the string may have other characters and newlines, but must include at least one occurrence of \n\n (adjacent newlines) to count as having a blank line.

Match any text that includes at least one empty line. An empty line is a line that contains no characters between two newline characters. The string can have any other content, but must contain a pair of consecutive newline characters (i.e., \n\n) to qualify.

In our app, we have a text area where the user enters multiple lines, each supposed to be a whole number (non-negative integer). We need to validate that every line is a valid number (digits only, no signs, no decimals). The text can have multiple lines separated by newlines. An empty text is not allowed. Each line must consist of one or more digits. Trailing newline? Typically not allowed; the last line should also be a number, so the string should not end with a newline unless followed by a number? Actually, if there's a trailing newline, the last line would be empty, which is not a number. So we disallow trailing newline. The whole string must consist of lines of digits separated by single newlines, with no empty lines and no trailing newline.

Only accept text where none of the lines have trailing spaces or tabs. That is, every line must end with a character that is not a space or tab. The string may contain multiple lines separated by newlines. Lines can be empty (which have no trailing whitespace). The whole string must not end with a space or tab before a newline or at the end.

items.description: Our changelog tooling groups commits automatically, so the subject line of every commit must conform to the Conventional Commits convention: a type, then an optional parenthesized scope, then an optional exclamation mark for breaking changes, then a colon and a space, then a non-empty subject. The allowed types are feat, fix, build, chore, ci, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, and revert, all in lowercase. The scope, when present, must be non-empty and contain only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, and slashes. The subject must not be empty. Only the shape of the line is checked, nothing about its meaning.

Our scheduler takes standard five-field cron expressions, but we only support the simple form. Each of the five fields separated by single spaces may be either a number, or a number followed by a hyphen and a larger number, or an asterisk, or a slash-annotated step. The allowed ranges per position are: minutes 0-59, hours 0-23, day-of-month 1-31, month 1-12, day-of-week 0-6. Steps may follow only a number or an asterisk, e.g. 5/15 or */15 only in the minute field; ignore this and simply allow a step in any field. A list of comma-separated values is not supported.
git branch name following a convention

In our Kubernetes tooling we let users type a resource name into a form. It must be a valid DNS-1123 label: lowercase alphanumeric characters or hyphens, must start and end with an alphanumeric character, and be at most 63 characters long. We do not accept underscores, dots, uppercase, leading or trailing hyphens, or consecutive hyphens.

Match a five-field cron expression where the fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, separated by single spaces. Each field may be a number, a range of two numbers separated by a hyphen, an asterisk, or a single value or asterisk followed by a slash and a step number. Range endpoints and step numbers must be plain numbers, and no lists are allowed.

Validate a Docker image reference with an optional tag. Rules:
- The image name may optionally start with a registry hostname, which is a domain name: one or more labels separated by dots, each label consisting of lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, not starting or ending with a hyphen. The registry hostname must be followed by a slash.
- After the optional registry, the repository name must be present. It consists of one or more path components separated by slashes. Each component must start and end with a lowercase letter or digit, and may contain lowercase letters, digits, periods, underscores, or hyphens in between. Consecutive separators (like // or ..) are not allowed.
- An optional tag may follow the repository name, introduced by a colon. The tag must start with a word character (letter, digit, or underscore) and may be followed by up to 127 word characters, periods, or hyphens. If present, the tag cannot be empty.
- The entire string must match from start to end.

Validate an npm package name, scoped or not. Rules:
- The name must be non-empty.
- It may be scoped, indicated by a leading @ symbol followed by a scope name and a slash, then the package name.
- The scope name (after @) must be non-empty and must consist only of URL-safe characters: letters (a-z, A-Z), digits, hyphens, underscores, and periods.
- The package name (the part after the optional scope and slash) must be non-empty and must consist only of URL-safe characters: letters (a-z, A-Z), digits, hyphens, underscores, and periods.
- The entire string must match from start to end.

Validate a simplified five-field cron expression. Fields are separated by single spaces. The fields, in order, are: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

items.description: Write a regex that matches a log line starting with a log level: either DEBUG, INFO, WARN, or ERROR, in uppercase, followed by a colon and a single space. The rest of the line can be any characters, including none.

We need to parse our web server's access log lines. Each line must start with the client IP address (four groups of up to three digits separated by dots, then a space), followed by the remote logname (a hyphen or a word of letters, digits, and underscores) and a space. Next is the authenticated user, which must be a hyphen or a word of letters, digits, and underscores, followed by a space. After that, the date and time enclosed in square brackets, containing exactly: day (two digits), slash, month abbreviated as three capital letters, slash, four-digit year, colon, two-digit hour, colon, two-digit minute, colon, two-digit second, space, plus or minus sign, and four-digit timezone offset. Then a closing bracket and a space. Next is the request line in double quotes: an uppercase HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, or PATCH), a space, a non-empty path consisting of any characters except spaces and double quotes, a space, and the HTTP version (HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1), all before the closing quote. Then a space. Next is the status code: exactly three digits. Then a space. Finally, the size in bytes: either a hyphen (if not applicable) or one or more digits. No other characters are allowed on the line.

Our error monitoring tool needs to extract stack trace frames from log lines. A valid stack trace frame line must start with optional whitespace, then the word 'at', then one or more spaces. After that, it must contain a function path: one or more segments separated by dots, where each segment is a sequence of letters, digits, underscores, or dollar signs, and the first character of each segment must not be a digit. The function path is followed by a space, then an opening parenthesis. After the parenthesis, the location part must be one of the following: (a) a file path (a sequence of characters that does not contain spaces or parentheses) followed by a colon, then one or more digits, then a colon, then one or more digits, and then a closing parenthesis; or (b) the word 'native' and a closing parenthesis; or (c) the word 'eval' followed by a space, an opening parenthesis, a file path with the same restrictions, a colon, digits, a colon, digits, and then a closing parenthesis for the file, then a closing parenthesis for the eval; or (d) the string '<anonymous>' and a closing parenthesis; or (e) the word 'new' followed by a space, then the same function path pattern, then a space, an opening parenthesis, a file path, a colon, digits, a colon, digits, and then two closing parentheses. The line must end immediately after all these parts, with no trailing characters (except possibly whitespace? No, exact end). No extra spaces or characters are allowed. The regex must match the whole line.

Match an HTTP status line that indicates a client or server error. The line must start with 'HTTP/' followed by a major version number (1 or 2), a period, and a minor version number (0, 1, or 2). Then a space, and a status code that is a three-digit number starting with 4 or 5 (i.e., from 400 to 599). Then a space, then a reason phrase consisting of one or more characters that are not line breaks (so any character except carriage return and line feed). The line must end after that. Do not match other status codes or malformed lines.

We need to identify log lines that contain an error code in the format 'ERR-' followed by exactly five digits. The error code can appear anywhere in the line, but it must be a standalone word: it must not be adjacent to any word character (letter, digit, or underscore) before 'ERR-' or after the five digits. The rest of the line can be anything.

items.description: nginx combined log line format

Our monitoring dashboard needs to flag any HTTP response status that indicates a client or server error. The status lines we process look like 'HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found' or 'HTTP/1.0 503 Service Unavailable'. Only lines where the status code starts with 4 or 5 should be flagged.

HTTP status line format: 'HTTP/<major>.<minor> <status-code> <reason-phrase>'. Major and minor are single digits. Status code is exactly three digits, and must be in the 400–599 range. Reason phrase is one or more characters and may contain spaces.

The line starts with the client IP address, followed by a space, then the remote logname (a hyphen if unknown), a space, the authenticated user (a hyphen if none), a space, and the timestamp enclosed in square brackets. After that, a space and the request line in double quotes, then a space, the HTTP status code (three digits), a space, the response size in bytes (digits or a hyphen), a space, the referrer in double quotes (may contain any characters except double quotes), a space, and the user agent in double quotes (also without double quotes). Use the combined log format.

Each field can be a single number, a range (two numbers separated by a dash), a comma-separated list of numbers or ranges, an asterisk, or a step value (a range or asterisk followed by a slash and a number).

An npm package name must be either unscoped or scoped. An unscoped name is a non-empty string of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, or periods. A scoped name starts with an '@', followed by a scope (same allowed characters), then a '/', then a package name (same allowed characters). The entire name must be at most 214 characters. items.description: We need to scan application log files and identify lines that are stack trace frames generated by our Node.js services (which run with the --enable-source-maps flag), so they can be linked to the corresponding source file in our error dashboard. A stack trace frame line always starts with at least one whitespace character, then the string "at " followed by a single space, then the function name which may be any sequence of characters (including spaces, dots, angle brackets), then a single space, then a path to a source file. The path can be an absolute or relative POSIX path, a Windows-style path using backslashes, or a file:// URL. After the path there is a colon, then a line number which is a positive integer (no leading zeros unless the number is zero), then another colon, then a column number which is also a positive integer. Optionally, the entire frame line may end with a parenthesized suffix that starts with "(" and ends with ")" and contains no newline characters; this suffix is often used for additional context. The line must not contain any other characters after the optional suffix. Only lines matching exactly this structure should be considered stack trace frames.

6. A quoted status code, which is exactly three digits, with no space inside the quotes.
7. An unquoted response size, which is either the single hyphen character or one or more digits.

A duration may be written in various units: milliseconds, seconds, or minutes, each optionally using the abbreviations ms, s, or m, or the full words milliseconds, seconds, or minutes, with any amount of whitespace between the number and the unit. The line is otherwise free-form, and if several durations appear, at least one of them must be above one second.","regex":"/^(?=[\s\S]*(?:\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:ms|milliseconds?|m|minutes?)\b|[2-9]\d*(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:s|seconds?)\b|1[1-9]\d*(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:s|seconds?)\b|1(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:s|seconds?)\b[^\d]*$|[2-9]\d*(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:s|seconds?)\b))[\s\S]*$/i"},{"slot":4,"description":"An application log line is valid only if it satisfies all of the following:

items.description: Our changelog bot reads pull-request titles and needs to tell whether a title follows our team convention. A valid title must begin with a Jira-style ticket key: one to four uppercase letters, a dash, then one to five digits. After the key there must be a colon and a single space. The rest is a description in imperative mood written in lowercase except that it may contain identifiers such as function names, mixed-case words, and code snippets are not allowed. For our purposes validate only that the description exists, starts with a lowercase ASCII letter, contains no uppercase letters other than inside bracketed scope words, and that any bracketed scope word must appear immediately after the colon-space and be one of api, ui, db, or cli followed by a colon and a space. The title may not end with a period.

Validate a Docker image reference suitable for a CI pipeline. Rules:
1. The reference consists of an optional registry host and path, a repository name, and an optional tag.
2. The registry host, when present, is a hostname followed by a slash, where the hostname is one or more dot-separated labels of letters, digits, and hyphens, each label starting and ending with a letter or digit, and the hostname may optionally end with a colon followed by a port number of one to five digits. The hostname must contain at least one dot or be localhost.
3. The path component, when present, is zero or more slash-separated segments, each segment being one or more lowercase letters, digits, underscores, periods, or double underscores, starting with a lowercase letter or digit.
4. The repository name is one or more slash-separated components of lowercase letters, digits, and separators, where a separator is one period, one underscore, or one or more hyphens, and each component starts and ends with a letter or digit.
5. The tag, when present, is a colon followed by one to 128 characters from the set of letters, digits, underscores, periods, and hyphens, and must not start with a period or hyphen.
6. The whole string is checked; no whitespace is permitted.

items.description: We enforce a branch naming scheme in our CI so every feature branch ties back to a ticket. A valid branch name must be all lowercase, consist of one or more segments separated by single forward slashes, and each segment may contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, with no leading or trailing hyphen and no consecutive hyphens. At least one segment must be exactly a ticket reference: the uppercase word 'TICKET' followed immediately by a hyphen and one or more digits. The ticket reference may appear as the final segment after one or more descriptive segments, or as the very first segment when the branch is only the ticket reference itself. Reject names containing uppercase letters, spaces, underscores, dots, backslashes, empty segments, a leading or trailing slash, or two consecutive slashes.

Our private registry proxies npm packages, and before publishing a package we must validate the name the user typed. A valid unscoped name is a single lowercase component; a valid scoped name is an at-sign, a scope component, a slash, and a package component. Every component must be between 1 and 214 characters long, must not start with a dot or an underscore, and may contain only lowercase letters, digits, and the characters hyphen, underscore, and dot; hyphens, underscores, and dots are allowed in the middle but not as the first character. The whole name must be lowercase and must contain no other characters, no leading or trailing whitespace, and no consecutive slashes.

When our deployment tooling generates Kubernetes manifests from user input, it asks the user for a resource name. The name must be a valid DNS subdomain: it is a series of one or more lowercase alphanumeric labels separated by single dots; each label starts and ends with a lowercase letter or digit and may contain hyphens in the middle, but no label may be empty and no two dots may be adjacent. The whole name must be at most 253 characters, and each label must be at most 63 characters. Reject names with uppercase letters, underscores, leading or trailing dots, leading or trailing hyphens in any label, and consecutive hyphens inside a label.

Our scheduler UI saves five-field cron expressions, and we validate the text the user enters before storing it. A valid expression has exactly five whitespace-separated fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week, in that order, with one or more spaces between fields. Minute is 0-59, hour is 0-23, day of month is 1-31, month is 1-12, and day of week is 0-6 where 0 means Sunday. Each field may be either a single number, or a range written as two numbers separated by a hyphen where the left number is less than or equal to the right number, or an asterisk meaning every value; the asterisk is not allowed as either endpoint of a range. Reject expressions with fewer or more than five fields, out-of-range numbers, ranges whose endpoints are not in order, empty fields, and any extra punctuation.

Our build system takes a container image reference typed by a developer and must accept Docker-style references. A valid reference is either a bare image name or an image name followed by an optional tag, but no digest. The image name is one or more lowercase path components separated by single slashes; each component starts and ends with a lowercase letter or digit and may contain dots and hyphens inside, but no uppercase letters, no underscores, no empty component, and no leading or trailing slash. The optional tag, if present, is a single colon immediately followed by one to 128 characters drawn from lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, underscores, dots, and hyphens, and the tag must not start with a dot or a hyphen. There must be no whitespace anywhere and the whole reference must be lowercase except inside the tag.

Case matters and the words "at", "Native Method" and "Unknown Source" are lowercase/uppercase exactly as written.

For traffic analytics we need to parse each line of our web server's access log. A line is the client IP address, then a space, then the identity field which is a dash, then a space, then the authenticated user name or a dash, then a space, then the request in double quotes (method, path and protocol separated by single spaces, no embedded quotes), then a space, then the three-digit status code, then a space, then the response size in bytes or a dash.

The scope name and the package name each must start with a letter or digit, may contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and dots, and must not begin with a dot or underscore. The total length must not exceed 214 characters. Encoding is not considered; the name must be lowercase.

We need to validate branch names that our team creates for feature work and hotfixes. A valid branch name must start with either 'feature/' or 'hotfix/', followed by a short description in lowercase kebab-case: one or more hyphen-separated words, where each word consists of lowercase letters, digits, or a single dot. Additionally, the branch name must not end with a hyphen or dot. The description part may contain slashes only if they separate words, but our convention forbids slashes in the description, so no extra slashes are allowed.

Validate a Conventional Commits title. Format: <type>[(<scope>)][!]: <description>. <type> is one of feat, fix, build, chore, ci, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, or revert, always lowercase. <scope> is optional, enclosed in parentheses, and consists of a non-empty sequence of lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, dots, or slashes. An optional exclamation mark (!) may follow the type or the closing parenthesis to indicate a breaking change. The colon and space (': ') are required after the type/scope/!. The <description> is a non-empty string of any characters except line terminators, and must not start or end with whitespace. No trailing whitespace is allowed.

For our Kubernetes manifests, every resource name must be a valid DNS-1123 subdomain: only lowercase alphanumeric characters, '-' or '.', and must start and end with an alphanumeric character. Names cannot exceed 253 characters.

Unscoped names must be at least one character, start with a letter or digit, and contain only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and dots. Scoped names start with '@', followed by a scope name (same character rules as unscoped, but must start with a letter or digit), then a slash '/', then a package name (same rules). items.description:
Validate an HTTP response status line, i.e. the first line of an HTTP response message. Rules:
- It must start with the protocol token 'HTTP' followed by a slash and the version, which is either '1.1' or '2' or '2.0'.
- Then a single space.
- Then a three-digit status code whose first digit is 4 or 5 and whose remaining two digits are 0-9.
- Then a single space.
- Then a reason phrase consisting of one or more printable ASCII characters (any character from space 0x20 through tilde 0x7E, i.e. letters, digits, punctuation and spaces, but no control characters).
- The whole string must match; no leading or trailing whitespace is allowed.

In our log viewer we only want to highlight lines that our application's own logger produced. Our logger always writes lines in the form LEVEL: message, where LEVEL is one of FATAL, ERROR, WARN or INFO and the message is the rest of the line. We must not match lines from third-party libraries that merely mention those words somewhere in the middle, so the level has to be at the very start of the line, uppercase exactly as listed, immediately followed by a colon and a single space, and then at least one character of message text. The whole line then counts as ours.

We want to detect standard web-server access-log lines in our log processing pipeline, matching the common combined format produced by Apache and nginx. A valid line looks like: the client IP address, then a space, then a dash (the ident field), then a space, then the authenticated user name or a dash if unauthenticated, then a space, then the request line enclosed in square brackets with the day, abbreviated month name and four-digit year, time, and timezone offset (e.g. +0000) inside, then a space, then the quoted HTTP request in double quotes, then a space, then the three-digit response status, then a space, then the response size in bytes or a dash, then a space, then the quoted referrer, then a space, and finally the quoted user agent. All of those parts must be present for a line to be recognized.

A log line is considered a standard entry if and only if it begins with one of the severity levels DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or CRITICAL in that exact uppercase form, and it is followed by a colon and exactly one space before the free-form message. The message may be any text (empty messages are allowed), and the case of the level must be exact, so lowercase variants are not accepted. The level must occur at the very beginning of the line.

Match any line that contains a Java-style stack trace frame, that is, the text 'at ' followed immediately by a fully qualified method reference: one or more dot-separated packages or classes, then a dot, then the method name, then an opening parenthesis up to the matching closing parenthesis.

A log line contains an error code exactly in the form ERR- followed by four digits, as a standalone token: it must be preceded by the start of the line or a non-word character, and followed by the end of the line or a non-word character.

A stack trace frame line looks like 'at functionName (filePath:line:column)' or 'at filePath:line:column'. The optional function name is followed by a space and a parenthesized location; for the second form the file path starts immediately after 'at '. The file path may be a path with slashes and dots, and the line and column are positive integers (no leading zeros unless zero itself).

An access log line in the common log format starts with the client IP address, followed by a space, a hyphen, a space, a user identifier (which may be a hyphen), a space, and then a timestamp enclosed in square brackets. The rest of the line is ignored.

Recognise a line whose first characters are the date in year-month-day order (four digits, hyphen, two digits, hyphen, two digits), then the letter T, then the time in hour:minute:second order with two digits each and colon separators. items.description: We need to verify that each line in our web server log file is a standard Apache or nginx combined log format entry. The combined log format has this structure: the client IP address, followed by a space, then a hyphen or username (a dash if not authenticated), then a space, then the username (dash if none), then a space, then the timestamp in square brackets: day/month/year:hour:minute:second timezone (day and month are two digits, year four digits, timezone is a plus or minus sign followed by four digits), then a space, then the request line in double quotes: method (e.g., GET, POST, HEAD, etc. capitalized), space, the request path (cannot contain spaces or double quotes), space, HTTP protocol version (HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1, but also HTTP/2.0 is seen in modern logs), then a space, the HTTP status code (three digits), then a space, the response size in bytes (a number or a dash if not recorded), then a space, the referrer in double quotes (may be a dash or a URL without spaces or double quotes), then a space, then the user agent in double quotes (may be a dash or any string without double quotes). The entire line must match this structure exactly. Write a regular expression that tests if a single line conforms to this combined log format. Note that the IP address could be IPv4 or IPv6, but for this check, assume it is a sequence of digits and dots (IPv4) to keep it simple; also, the timestamp is not checked for actual calendar validity, only the format. The line may contain any characters inside the quoted strings except unescaped double quotes. The log line should not have leading or trailing spaces.

The line must contain a stack trace frame in the standard Java format: it starts with optional whitespace, then the string 'at', then one or more spaces, then a fully qualified class name (consisting of one or more identifiers separated by dots; each identifier starts with a letter, underscore, or dollar sign, followed by letters, digits, underscores, or dollar signs), then a dot, then a method name (same identifier rules), then an opening parenthesis, then either the file name followed by a colon and a line number (the file name ends with '.java', '.kt', '.scala', or '.groovy'), or the string 'Native Method', or the string 'Unknown Source', then a closing parenthesis. The line must start with optional whitespace and end immediately after the closing parenthesis. The entire line must match this pattern; no extra content before or after is allowed.
Match a line that contains an error code like ERR-1234 where the number has exactly four digits.
line with duration >1s like 1.5s or 2s

We are parsing our web server access logs to monitor traffic, and we need to ensure that each log entry follows the common log format or combined log format that our server produces. The log lines should be from Apache or nginx, and we want to validate their structure. The format we expect is: the client's IP address (IPv4), followed by a space, then the identity (a hyphen if not available), then a space, then the authenticated user (a hyphen if none), then a space, then the date and time in square brackets in the format day/month/year:hour:minute:second timezone, where day and month are two digits, year is four digits, and timezone is a plus or minus followed by four digits. After that, there is a space, then the request line in double quotes: the method (e.g., GET, POST, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, etc., in uppercase, but we'll accept any uppercase letters), a space, the requested resource (which can be any sequence of characters except double quotes and spaces; it usually starts with a slash but can be '*'), a space, and the protocol version (HTTP/1.0 or HTTP/1.1). Then a space, then the status code (three digits), then a space, then the size in bytes (a number or a hyphen). Optionally, there can be more fields: a referrer in double quotes (which may be a hyphen or a URL without spaces or double quotes) and a user agent in double quotes (which may be a hyphen or any string without double quotes). The optional part starts with a space before the referrer. The entire line must match this pattern. We do not care about the actual IP address values, just that they look like IPv4 addresses. Also, we don't validate the date for correctness, just the format. The log line should not have leading or trailing spaces.
